Tip Procedure: Resolve And Synchronize In The Container



scripts/mdg-healthshed-clinic-data exec uvr lock

# One-time migration for an existing binary library; preserve it for rollback.
# Repeat after a native ABI change, with R sessions stopped.
if test -d .uvr/library; then
  backup=".uvr/cache/library-before-source-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
  test ! -e "$backup"
  mkdir -p .uvr/cache
  mv .uvr/library "$backup"
fi

# Namespace compiled packages by the image's concrete native environment.
native_lock_sha=$(scripts/mdg-healthshed-clinic-data exec \
  sha256sum /opt/spack-environment/spack.lock | awk '{print $1}')
test "${#native_lock_sha}" -eq 64
scripts/mdg-healthshed-clinic-data exec env \
  UVR_PACKAGES_DIR="/work/.uvr/cache/spack-packages/${native_lock_sha}" \
  uvr sync --frozen --no-binary
scripts/mdg-healthshed-clinic-data exec uvr activate --write-shim
Source builds are the accepted policy for this Spack runtime. The source flag is supported by the pinned uvr 0.4.6. Its implementation first skips packages already installed at the locked version, even with --no-binary or --ignore-cache. Preserving and replacing the existing library is therefore necessary for the initial binary-to-source migration.
The documented UVR_PACKAGES_DIR override is scoped to this installation command: it isolates compiled source-cache entries by native lock hash without changing the image, runner, activation, default project library, download cache, or another project’s packages. uvr’s source cache key includes R/version/source identity but not the full GDAL/GEOS/PROJ build. A separate cache namespace is needed after native ABI changes; do not delete the shared global cache or create compatibility SONAME symlinks. Reuse the same command, native lock hash, and --no-binary for later synchronization; routine syncs do not need the library-backup step.
These behaviors were checked against the pinned sync implementation, cache key, and supported environment variables.
Commit uvr.lock only after successful resolution through the built runtime. Use uvr r pin only when an additional exact .r-version pin is intentional; do not generate that optional file outside uvr.
Run scripts through uvr run. For an interactive session, enter the container shell and source .uvr/activate; that shim asks uvr to resolve the current project environment instead of storing hard-coded paths.








Tip Procedure: Recover An Incomplete Compiled Package



shared object 'duckdb.so' not found identifies the R package’s own compiled module. A successful source installation of duckdb produces that module and installs the R code alongside it. Adding a Spack DuckDB CLI or a separate libduckdb.so does not install the R bindings. This differs from a missing libudunits2.so.0, which is an external dependency of an existing R module.
The observed duckdb 2.0.0 directory contained DESCRIPTION, an empty libs/, and no R/. That is an incomplete installation, not evidence of a missing native Spack root. uvr 0.4.6’s version-only installed-package check can skip this directory and fail later when compiling duckplyr. Its source installer also disables staged installation and the final load test. Retain the failed package and the earlier compilation log before retrying; the downstream error does not establish why the earlier build stopped.
With no installer or R session using the library, recover just the incomplete package, then synchronize from the existing lock. This does not re-resolve versions or clear the shared package cache:
broken=".uvr/cache/duckdb-incomplete-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
test ! -e "$broken"
mkdir -p .uvr/cache
mv .uvr/library/duckdb "$broken"
native_lock_sha=$(scripts/mdg-healthshed-clinic-data exec \
  sha256sum /opt/spack-environment/spack.lock | awk '{print $1}')
test "${#native_lock_sha}" -eq 64
scripts/mdg-healthshed-clinic-data exec env \
  UVR_PACKAGES_DIR="/work/.uvr/cache/spack-packages/${native_lock_sha}" \
  MAKEFLAGS=-j1 uvr sync --frozen --no-binary --ignore-cache --timeout 2h
scripts/mdg-healthshed-clinic-data exec Rscript scripts/check-tabular-runtime.R
DuckDB compiles a substantial C++ engine. The recovery uses one compiler job and an explicit timeout to limit concurrent build memory and allow the build to finish. If it fails, inspect the first compiler/linker error in the DuckDB install log before retrying or changing infrastructure. For an isolated diagnostic build, R CMD INSTALL --library=<temporary-library> <locked-source> uses R’s default staged installation and load tests; validate it before promoting its package directory into the project library.








Tip Procedure: Emit The DuckDB And Parquet Runtime Check



This checks the installed R module before loading either namespace, then executes a grouped SQL query through duckplyr and round-trips a synthetic Parquet file. It reads no research data or targets store.
# Run through scripts/mdg-healthshed-clinic-data exec Rscript.
local({
  package <- find.package("duckdb", quiet = TRUE)
  if (!length(package)) stop("The duckdb R package is not installed.")
  module <- file.path(package, "libs", paste0("duckdb", .Platform$dynlib.ext))
  if (!file.exists(module)) {
    stop("Incomplete duckdb R installation: missing ", module,
         ". Reinstall the locked R package; see infrastructure page 14.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  loadNamespace("duckdb")
  loadNamespace("duckplyr")
  cat("duckdb:", as.character(utils::packageVersion("duckdb")), "\n")
  cat("duckplyr:", as.character(utils::packageVersion("duckplyr")), "\n")
  cat("Module:", normalizePath(module), "\n")
  source <- duckplyr::read_sql_duckdb(
    "SELECT k, sum(v) AS total FROM (VALUES ('a',1.5),('a',2.5),('b',NULL::DOUBLE)) t(k,v) GROUP BY k ORDER BY k",
    prudence = "stingy")
  output <- tempfile("duckdb-runtime-", fileext = ".parquet")
  on.exit(unlink(output), add = TRUE)
  duckplyr::compute_parquet(source, output)
  actual <- duckplyr::read_parquet_duckdb(output, prudence = "stingy") |>
    dplyr::collect() |>
    dplyr::arrange(k)
  stopifnot(identical(actual$k, c("a", "b")),
            identical(actual$total, c(4, NA_real_)))
  message("Tabular runtime accepted: DuckDB R module, duckplyr SQL, and Parquet round trip.")
})








Tip Procedure: Emit The Synthetic Spatial Runtime Check



Run this after source synchronization. It reads no research inputs and does not build targets. It reports package/engine versions and s2 state, tests unit conversion, GEOS repair/union/relations, graph components, CRS round trips, spherical area, GDAL shapefile/GeoPackage I/O, fuzzy matching, and headless map exports. The temporary GeoPackage only checks the SQLite-enabled driver; it does not establish a new pipeline artifact format. Scientific parity and legacy tmap-call migration remain separate stage-5 tests.
# Run through scripts/mdg-healthshed-clinic-data exec Rscript.
# Synthetic runtime acceptance only: no staged data or targets store access.
local({
  required <- c("sf", "units", "s2", "igraph", "fuzzyjoin", "stringdist",
                "ggplot2", "ggpubr", "MetBrewer", "tmap", "readxl")
  failures <- vapply(required, function(package) {
    tryCatch({ loadNamespace(package); "" }, error = conditionMessage)
  }, character(1))
  if (any(nzchar(failures))) {
    stop("Geospatial runtime is not ready:\n",
         paste(names(failures)[nzchar(failures)], failures[nzchar(failures)],
               sep = ": ", collapse = "\n"), call. = FALSE)
  }
  print(data.frame(package = required,
                   version = vapply(required, function(p) as.character(utils::packageVersion(p)), character(1))))
  print(sf::sf_extSoftVersion())
  cat("sf_use_s2:", sf::sf_use_s2(), "\n")
  cat("UDUNITS2_XML_PATH:", Sys.getenv("UDUNITS2_XML_PATH"), "\n")
  stopifnot(as.numeric(units::set_units(units::set_units(1, "km"), "m")) == 1000)

  scratch <- tempfile("geospatial-runtime-")
  dir.create(scratch)
  on.exit(unlink(scratch, recursive = TRUE), add = TRUE)
  geometry <- sf::st_as_sfc(c(
    "POLYGON ((0 0, 1 0, 1 1, 0 1, 0 0))",
    "POLYGON ((1 0, 2 0, 2 1, 1 1, 1 0))",
    "POLYGON ((4 0, 5 0, 5 1, 4 1, 4 0))"
  ), crs = 3857)
  shapes <- sf::st_sf(id = 1:3, geometry = geometry)
  stopifnot(all(sf::st_is_valid(shapes)),
            abs(as.numeric(sf::st_area(sf::st_union(geometry))) - 3) < 1e-8)
  adjacency <- sf::st_relate(geometry, pattern = "F***1****", sparse = FALSE)
  graph <- igraph::graph_from_adjacency_matrix(adjacency, mode = "undirected")
  stopifnot(igraph::components(graph)$no == 2L)
  bowtie <- sf::st_as_sfc("POLYGON ((0 0, 1 1, 1 0, 0 1, 0 0))", crs = 3857)
  stopifnot(all(sf::st_is_valid(sf::st_make_valid(bowtie))))

  point <- sf::st_sfc(sf::st_point(c(47, -19)), crs = 4326)
  back <- sf::st_transform(sf::st_transform(point, 32738), 4326)
  stopifnot(max(abs(sf::st_coordinates(back) - sf::st_coordinates(point))) < 1e-6)
  spherical <- s2::s2_geog_from_text("POLYGON ((47 -19, 48 -19, 48 -18, 47 -18, 47 -19))")
  stopifnot(is.finite(s2::s2_area(spherical)), s2::s2_area(spherical) > 0)
  for (extension in c("shp", "gpkg")) {
    path <- file.path(scratch, paste0("shapes.", extension))
    sf::st_write(shapes, path, quiet = TRUE)
    restored <- sf::st_read(path, quiet = TRUE)
    stopifnot(nrow(restored) == 3L, sf::st_crs(restored) == sf::st_crs(shapes),
              all(sf::st_equals(restored, shapes, sparse = FALSE)[cbind(1:3, 1:3)]))
  }
  matched <- fuzzyjoin::stringdist_inner_join(
    data.frame(name = "Ambato"), data.frame(name = "Ambato"),
    by = "name", method = "cosine", max_dist = 0)
  stopifnot(nrow(matched) == 1L,
            stringdist::stringdist("Ambato", "Ambato", method = "cosine") == 0)

  stopifnot(capabilities("cairo"))
  plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(shapes) + ggplot2::geom_sf(
    ggplot2::aes(fill = factor(id))) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = MetBrewer::met.brewer("Renoir", 3))
  png <- file.path(scratch, "geometry.png")

title: 14  Run the Project Environment
text:
The runner is the only place that selects the image, cleans the host environment, and binds writable project state. Interactive shells, explicit command execution, and Slurm all consume this same boundary.






Important Prerequisite: Confirm The Runtime Image



Build the image from the preceding pages or set MDG_HEALTHSHED_CLINIC_DATA_IMAGE in containers/runtime/local.env.









Tip Procedure: Emit The Environment Runner



#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

project_dir=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)

usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage:
  mdg-healthshed-clinic-data [shell [SHELL_OPTION...]]
  mdg-healthshed-clinic-data exec COMMAND [ARG...]

With no arguments, open a shell in /work. Commands must use the explicit
`exec` subcommand.
EOF
}

action=${1:-shell}
if (( $# > 0 )); then
  shift
fi

case "${action}" in
  shell) ;;
  exec)
    if (( $# == 0 )); then
      echo "The exec subcommand requires a command." >&2
      usage >&2
      exit 64
    fi
    ;;
  -h|--help)
    usage
    exit 0
    ;;
  *)
    echo "Unknown subcommand: ${action}" >&2
    usage >&2
    exit 64
    ;;
esac

local_env="${project_dir}/containers/runtime/local.env"
if [[ -f "${local_env}" ]]; then
  set -a
  source "${local_env}"
  set +a
fi

runtime=${CONTAINER_RUNTIME:-apptainer}
if ! command -v "${runtime}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  runtime=singularity
fi
command -v "${runtime}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || {
  echo "Neither apptainer nor singularity is available." >&2
  exit 127
}

image=${MDG_HEALTHSHED_CLINIC_DATA_IMAGE:-"${project_dir}/artifacts/containers/mdg-healthshed-clinic-data.sif"}
test -r "${image}" || {
  echo "Container image not readable: ${image}" >&2
  echo "Build it from the Infrastructure pages or set MDG_HEALTHSHED_CLINIC_DATA_IMAGE." >&2
  exit 1
}

runtime_options=(
  --cleanenv
  --bind "${project_dir}:/work"
  --pwd /work
)

case "${action}" in
  shell)
    exec "${runtime}" shell "${runtime_options[@]}" "$@" "${image}"
    ;;
  exec)
    exec "${runtime}" exec "${runtime_options[@]}" "${image}" "$@"
    ;;
esac

The hand-delivered gdn_datafreeze_may2025/madagascar_clinic_data_cleaning.zip is the sole source of truth for the existing-wave migration. Its scientific inputs and comparison outputs come exclusively from this ZIP. The separate new-wave deliveries enter through page 26’s Stagecoach inventory and file branches. Both deliveries and maximum reduction were authorized on 2026-11-08; this page still reads only the ZIP.






Important Prerequisite: Confirm Staging Authority



On 2026-11-06 the researcher selected the ZIP supplied by hand as the fixed input freeze and migration baseline. The previously staged Google Drive tree is a periodically refreshed rclone mirror and can drift. It is excluded from the pipeline, even when its files are newer. Existing Drive staging links may remain on disk, but no existing-wave inventory scans or scientific readers use them. The explicitly scoped new-wave branch remains separate from this inventory.
The Stagecoach manifest declares the hand-delivered ZIP for this migration and two separate, narrowly scoped new-wave survey items for page 26. This page’s inventory still consumes only the ZIP. Tip Procedure: Select And Extract Reviewed Archive Inputs



Keep the existing path-based W3 and mapping readers, but supply them only with unmodified source members extracted from the tracked ZIP. Select all W3 CSVs and the exact reviewed mapping/identity sources. Other stages continue to read their exact members directly from this same archive. The extracted copies retain the original filenames and formats under data/intermediates/archive_sources/; they are source copies, not new curated products. They are tracked files and may be recreated from the ZIP.
Return only the members selected in this invocation, never a scan of the extraction directory. Old extractions and Drive files cannot enter the graph.
s0_pipeline_archive_members_fn <- function(archive) {
  members <- utils::unzip(archive, list = TRUE)$Name
  root <- "madagascar_clinic_data_cleaning/data/raw/"
  w3 <- members[startsWith(members, paste0(root, "from Symphonia/RMA_W3_FULL/")) &
                  endsWith(members, ".csv")]
  reviewed <- paste0(root, c(
    "from Symphonia/mapping GESIS DHIS questions - mapping DHIS2 GESIS 2010 2022.csv",
    "symphonia_verified/CSB1 CSB2 PUBLIC PRIVATE.xlsx",
    "symphonia_verified/gesis_missing_uid_in_mapping.xlsx",
    "symphonia_verified/VERIFIER fs_uid_year_with_multiple_gesis.csv",
    "symphonia_verified/VERIFIER clinic_codes_in_gesis_but_not_in_mapping.csv",
    "symphonia_verified/GESIS_snips_public_multipleLongGESIS VERIFIED.csv"
  ))
  if (!length(w3) || any(!reviewed %in% members)) {
    stop("The ZIP is missing required W3 or reviewed mapping/identity inputs.")
  }
  selected <- sort(c(w3, reviewed), method = "radix")
  stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(selected), all(vapply(selected, function(x) sum(members == x), 0L) == 1L),
            !any(grepl("^/|(^|/)\\.\\.(/|$)", selected)))
  selected
}

s0_pipeline_archive_inputs_fn <- function(archive, output_dir) {
  members <- s0_pipeline_archive_members_fn(archive)
  dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  paths <- utils::unzip(archive, files = members, exdir = output_dir, overwrite = TRUE)
  stopifnot(length(paths) == length(members), all(file.exists(paths)))
  # Include the tracked ZIP for the existing exact-archive selectors in later stages.
  c(archive, paths)
}

title: 17  Curate the Healthshed Clinic Data
text:
This page declares the Wave 3 preparation targets tangled by _targets.R.






Important Prerequisite: Approve The Curation Contract



The source-inspection page must first record the source schema, record grain, stable keys, pre-/post-DHIS2 boundary, missing-value semantics, validation rules, and disclosure controls.








Tip Procedure: Declare The Parquet Transformation Boundary



Declare the shared file-to-file transformation used by this page and by the clinic-month inventory. Each caller supplies its dependencies and output path.
The helper below opens Parquet inputs with automatic materialization into R disabled, applies the supplied transformation, and writes the result through DuckDB. Only the output path crosses the target boundary. Input paths, output paths, and transformation dependencies stay explicit at each call site.
s0_pipeline_parquet_transform_fn <- function(
  input_paths, output_path, transform, read_options = list()
) {
  input_paths <- unname(as.character(input_paths))
  stopifnot(
    length(input_paths) > 0L,
    all(file.exists(input_paths)),
    length(output_path) == 1L, !is.na(output_path), nzchar(output_path),
    is.function(transform)
  )

  relation <- duckplyr::read_parquet_duckdb(
    input_paths,
    prudence = "stingy",
    options = read_options
  )
  result <- transform(relation)

  dir.create(dirname(output_path), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  duckplyr::compute_parquet(result, output_path)
  output_path
}








Tip Procedure: Read One Raw RMA File With Explicit Types



In this first section of the script, we take raw files and prepare them by aggregating them into a tracked Parquet file, one row per clinic-year-month, and one column per health outcome-age-sex.
Applies only to 2020-2022 data.
We’ve also opted-in to using DuckDB via the duckplyr package to avoid in-memory limitations.
library(targets)
library(readr)
library(openxlsx)
library(duckplyr)
library(cli)

tar_load(s0_pipeline_inputs_raw_chr)
We have a variable number of missing values in our first rows of data, so we’ll need to ensure they don’t get read as logical NAs. The duckplyr options list allows us to force DOUBLE and VARCHAR types:
The archived CSVs also use literal NA for missing values. The legacy readr::read_csv() reader recognizes both empty fields and NA as missing; set DuckDB’s nullstr explicitly to preserve that rule before converting measurements to DOUBLE. Otherwise row-count diagnostics can succeed while the Parquet write fails when it evaluates the measurement columns. Missing values remain null, including in entirely missing numeric columns.
s0_clinic_RMA_read_nonlogical_fn <- function(filepath){

  readr_spec <- spec_csv(filepath) 
  spec_names <- names(readr_spec$cols)

  readr_spec %>%
    as.character() %>%
    str_split_1("") %>%
    tibble(spec = .) %>%
    mutate(
      name = spec_names,
      duckdb_dtype = case_when(
        str_detect(name, regex("description", ignore_case = TRUE)) ~ "VARCHAR",
        spec == "c" ~ "VARCHAR",
        spec == "d" ~ "DOUBLE",
        spec == "l" ~ "DOUBLE",
        .default = "DOUBLE"
      )
    ) %>%
    select(name, duckdb_dtype) %>%
    deframe() -> duckdb_spec

  
  # Set the CSV dialect explicitly. Auto-detection samples only the first
  # rows, so a quoted comma appearing later can otherwise be misclassified as
  # an extra column.
  read_csv_duckdb(
    filepath,
    options = list(
      types = list(duckdb_spec),
      nullstr = list(c("", "NA")),
      delim = ",",
      quote = "\"",
      escape = "\""
    )
  ) %>%
    return()
  
}








Tip Procedure: Declare The Clinic-Month Maximum Reduction



Define the reducer shared by the per-file and cross-file aggregation stages. Missing grouping keys fail before a result can be written.
The reductions below use operations that duckplyr translates to DuckDB. DuckDB’s MAX() ignores null values and returns null for an all-null group, which preserves the behavior of the previous max_or_na() helper without materializing columns in R.
s0_clinic_RMA_summarise_group_max_fn <- function(df) {
  grouping_columns <- c("organisationunitid", "periodname")
  missing_grouping_columns <- setdiff(grouping_columns, names(df))
  if (length(missing_grouping_columns)) {
    stop(
      "Cannot calculate clinic-month maxima; missing grouping column(s): ",
      paste(missing_grouping_columns, collapse = ", ")
    )
  }

  df |>
    summarise(
      across(
        -all_of(grouping_columns),
        ~ max(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
      ),
      .by = all_of(grouping_columns)
    )
}








Tip Procedure: Write One Reduced Parquet Branch



Read one source file, remove redundant columns, compute its clinic-month maxima, and write the branch artifact. The small row-count diagnostics are collected for the execution log; the measurement table stays in DuckDB.
s0_clinic_RMA_process_csv_fn <- function(csv_path, output_path=here("data/intermediates"), drop_cols = c("organisationunitcode", "organisationunitdescription")) {
  stopifnot(length(csv_path) == 1L, file.exists(csv_path))
  
  cli_alert_info(paste("Working on:", csv_path))
  
  # Read file with type-safe reader
  temp_df <- s0_clinic_RMA_read_nonlogical_fn(csv_path)
  
  # Drop the extra columns if they exist
  temp_df <- temp_df %>%
    select(-any_of(drop_cols))
  
  # Calculate diagnostics in DuckDB and collect only the two scalar results.
  file_stats <- temp_df |>
    summarise(
      group_rows = n(),
      .by = c(organisationunitid, periodname)
    ) |>
    summarise(
      rows = sum(group_rows),
      duplicate_rows = sum(group_rows - 1L)
    ) |>
    collect()

  cli_alert_info(paste(
    "Successfully created dataframe for", csv_path, "with shape",
    file_stats$rows[[1]], "x", length(names(temp_df))
  ))
  cli_alert_info(paste(
    "Number of duplicate clinic-month-year records:",
    file_stats$duplicate_rows[[1]]
  ))
  
  # Description fields are assigned VARCHAR when the CSV relation is created.
  result = s0_clinic_RMA_summarise_group_max_fn(temp_df)
  
  dir.create(dirname(output_path), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  compute_parquet(result, output_path)

  output_path
}
s0_clinic_RMA_process_csv_fn() intentionally accepts exactly one path, and never holds other input tables in memory. _targets.R selects the RMA_W3_FULL paths in s0_clinic_RMA_W3_raw_paths_chr, then declares one file-tracking branch per path in s0_clinic_RMA_W3_raw_csv. The Parquet writer maps over those tracked file branches outside this notebook. That makes each CSV independently schedulable and means the branch artifacts contain parquet files rather than raw csvs. Dynamic branching enables parallel execution; the approved Slurm allocation and selected targets backend determine how many branches run concurrently.
The second reduction in _targets.R combines the smaller branch summaries and takes the clinic-month maximum again. This is equivalent to taking the maximum over the fully combined raw data because maximum is associative:
[ () = ((), , ()) ]
This two-stage reduction was introduced after the raw-table aggregation was OOM-killed with a 120 GiB Slurm allocation. It is a memory-scaling change, not a change to the numeric maximum rule. The current reducer retains the prior rule for every non-grouping field; a later curation decision should define field-specific behavior for names, descriptions, and codes rather than treating a lexicographic character maximum as scientific metadata.






WarningWhy aggregation stays in DuckDB



The per-file reductions completed, but the final target was OOM-killed in a 120 GiB Slurm allocation. The diagnostic evidence is that files can have zero duplicate clinic-month keys. In that situation, a per-file group maximum has nearly the same cardinality as the input, so the previous R-based final target needed to materialize all branch summaries at once. Increasing the requested memory is not the next proposed experiment.
The per-file target now implements a disk-backed DuckDB/duckplyr boundary. Its stages are:

preserve the existing one-file CSV reading, UTF-8, and type-normalization behavior;
execute each per-file clinic-month MAX reduction in DuckDB;
write each branch result to Parquet without materializing it in R.

The final target below reads all branch Parquet paths as one DuckDB relation, executes the final clinic-month reduction, and persists that result through another file target.
The aim is to preserve the original code’s transformation logic as closely as possible. The change is the execution engine and storage boundary, not a redesign of the data-cleaning rules. Before implementation, the output schema and reducer for metadata fields must be made explicit: numeric measures use maximum, whereas names, descriptions, and codes require a domain-specific rule. DuckDB and duckplyr are declared runtime dependencies.










Tip Procedure: Combine The Reduced Branches



Apply the same reduction to the branch files to obtain one tracked group-maximum artifact. No raw measurement table needs to be collected into R.
Calculate the group maxima across all branch artifacts with the shared helper. union_by_name preserves columns that occur in only some source files.
#| format: file
s0_clinic_RMA_W3_group_max_parquet <- s0_pipeline_parquet_transform_fn(
  input_paths = s0_clinic_RMA_W3_within_file_max_parquet,
  output_path = here("data/intermediates/RMA_W3_group_max.parquet"),
  transform = s0_clinic_RMA_summarise_group_max_fn,
  read_options = list(union_by_name = TRUE)
)








Tip Procedure: Crosswalk with GESIS Data



Our next step is to crosswalk the clinic data with GESIS DHIS data to get the exact questions for each measure.
#| format: file
s0_gesis_xwalk_raw_csv <- s0_pipeline_inputs_raw_chr |>
  str_subset("mapping DHIS2 GESIS 2010 2022")
s0_gesis_xwalk_nonmissing_uid_df <- read_csv(s0_gesis_xwalk_raw_csv) |>
  select(UID...12, code_fs, TYPE, FS) |>
  rename(organisationunitid = UID...12) |> #correct the naming of organisationunitid
  distinct() |>                            #tidy up missingness
  filter(!is.na(organisationunitid))








Tip Procedure: Write The Cleaned Wave 3 Table



Use the descriptive crosswalk and the reviewed period-specific substitutions to produce the cleaned Parquet artifact.
Lastly, we left_join the RMA wave 3 data with this crosswalk on Organisation. The last bit of cleaning correctly maps diagnoses that changed names slightly between wave 3 subwaves
#| format: file
s0_clinic_RMA_W3_clean_parquet <- s0_pipeline_parquet_transform_fn(
  input_paths = s0_clinic_RMA_W3_group_max_parquet,
  output_path = here("data/intermediates/clinic_RMA_W3_clean.parquet"),
  transform = function(relation) {
    relation |>
      left_join(as_duckdb_tibble(s0_gesis_xwalk_nonmissing_uid_df), by = "organisationunitid") |>
      mutate(
        # rows of AME where periodcode > 202300 should be values of AME prem;
        `T13: AME 0-6 mois` = if_else(
          periodcode > 202300,  `T13: AME premiere heure 0-6 mois`, `T13: AME 0-6 mois`
        ),
        # etc
        `T13: AME 1ère heure` = if_else(
          periodcode > 202300, `T13: AME premiere heure 1ère heure`, `T13: AME 1ère heure`
        ),
        `MIDs pour groupe à risque (migrants/réfugiés/personnes déplacées)` = if_else(
          periodcode > 202300, `CHU CHRR T26 MIDs pour groupe à risque (migrants/réfugiés/personnes déplacées)`, `MIDs pour groupe à risque (migrants/réfugiés/personnes déplacées)`
        )
      ) |>
      # remove redundant
      select(
        -any_of(c(
          "T13: AME premiere heure 0-6 mois",
          "T13: AME premiere heure 1ère heure",
          "CHU CHRR T26 MIDs pour groupe à risque (migrants/réfugiés/personnes déplacées)"
        ))
      ) |>
      mutate(V1 = row_number() - 1L) |>
      select(V1, everything())
  }
)


Important: there is a chance that the assignment of V1 to row number doesn’t work here, due to the fact that the data is now in a Parquet and row numbers are only computed at evaluation time.

  `most recent archived data` = old_w3 |> dplyr::count(periodcode, name = "rows") |>
    dplyr::collect() |> dplyr::mutate(periodcode = as.integer(periodcode)),
  `current pipeline` = new_w3 |> dplyr::count(periodcode, name = "rows") |>
    dplyr::collect() |> dplyr::mutate(periodcode = as.integer(periodcode)),
  .id = "source"
) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = source, values_from = rows, values_fill = 0L) |>
  dplyr::mutate(difference = `current pipeline` - `most recent archived data`) |>
  dplyr::arrange(periodcode) |>
  print(n = Inf)
An absent period contributes zero rows; difference is current minus archived.
Diagnose row coverage before comparing measurement values.
Run the read-only diagnostic in an authorized analysis session. It compares the most recent archived data with the current pipeline, inventories both raw source trees, and checks that their distinct clinic-month keys survive into their respective prepared outputs. It then compares the legacy readr key reader with the stored DuckDB reader on the selected separate-year delivery, verifies the crosswalk’s content identity, and reconciles the final row-count difference using the join multiplicities. It builds no targets and changes no pipeline outputs. Keep its data-derived summaries outside rendered HTML.
scripts/mdg-healthshed-clinic-data exec Rscript scripts/diagnose-w3-row-coverage.R
The legacy script and current implementation differ at these boundaries:









Boundary
Legacy script 0
Current DuckDB pipeline
Diagnostic implication




Raw file selection
Recursively lists .csv files below its local RMA_W3_FULL directory.
Selects staged inventory paths containing RMA_W3_FULL; tracks and processes each file separately.
Compare actual selected paths and file versions before attributing differences to an engine. Separate-year and combined-year exports need not contain the same records.


CSV parsing
readr::spec_csv() with inferred logical collectors replaced by col_number(), followed by readr::read_csv().
Uses the inferred specification to request VARCHAR or DOUBLE, forces description fields to VARCHAR, and sets CSV delimiter/quoting explicitly.
Types, missing-value interpretation, and character parsing require comparison. The diagnostic projects the grouping keys and tests both readers on identical files.


Maximum reduction
Combines all raw tables in R, then takes one data.table maximum per clinic ID and period name. Converts -Inf results to missing.
Takes per-file maxima, unions Parquet schemas by column name, then takes maxima again in DuckDB. All-null SQL maxima remain null.
Both use the same grouping key. Associativity preserves numeric maxima on identical parsed inputs; verify key conservation separately from value/type equivalence.


Facility crosswalk
Selects UID, code, type, and name; removes exact duplicates and missing UIDs; left-joins on UID.
Performs the same selection and join through DuckDB.
Several distinct crosswalk records may match one UID and expand a clinic-month into multiple rows. Compare multiplicity, not just distinct key counts.


Final corrections and storage
Uses indexed assignments for the period-specific diagnosis substitutions, adds a sequential V1, and writes CSV.
Uses if_else() for the same substitutions, adds row_number() - 1, and writes Parquet.
These operations do not deliberately filter rows. Row order and export indices are not stable alignment keys; types and missing-period behavior need separate value checks.



The source decision is settled: reproduce the hand-delivered May 2025 ZIP. Use its separate-year raw files for W3 preparation and its archived outputs for comparison. The synced Drive delivery is excluded. Previously built Drive-based targets require rebuilding before this comparison is meaningful.

title: 18  Clean the DHIS2–GESIS Mapping
text:
This page translates the reviewed DHIS2–GESIS mapping-cleaning workflow into successive targets. The stage boundaries separate source reads, reviewed corrections, validation queries, and persistence so each decision remains auditable while the execution becomes reproducible.






WarningPreserve reviewed decisions while modernizing



The transformations below preserve the reviewed mapping decisions from the legacy workflow. Each assigned object is a pipeline target. Diagnostic chunks in the final check are deliberately unassigned: they inspect completed targets without adding check-only objects to the graph. The authoring render does not execute them.








Important Prerequisite: Retain The Reviewed Source Evidence



The original mapping CSV and the four manually reviewed workbooks or CSVs must remain available with their provenance intact. Before optimizing a stage, record its input schema, expected row-count change, join cardinality, and the review decision represented by each correction.








Tip Procedure: Load The Mapping Tools



Load the packages used by the mapping transformations and their diagnostic queries. Scientific execution still occurs through the targets graph.
#| eval: true
#| include: false
library(targets)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(assertr)
library(stringr)








Tip Procedure: Stage 1 — Read And Filter The Source Mapping



This stage reads the base mapping, and assigns names to the four UID levels. It removes the year 2022 and Belalanda from the list.
Interestingly, this reads in the crosswalk file separately from the previous stage. We have to keep an eye on that…
s1_gesis_xwalk_filtered_df <- read.csv(s0_gesis_xwalk_raw_csv) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  rename(region_uid = UID, 
         district_uid = `UID.1`,
         commune_uid = `UID.2`, 
         fs_uid = `UID.3`) |>
  filter(cAnnee != "2022" & code_fs != "Belalanda") %>%
  verify(nrow(.) == 34812)  








Tip Procedure: Stages 2–3 — Correct GESIS Codes And Fill The Known UID



This stage loads the reviewed corrections, checks UID consistency for both the old and corrected codes, applies the corrected GESIS code, and fills the known UID for GESIS code 630151027.
#| format: file
# 2) bits out of range ------
# Some clinic GESIS codes have the type or public/private bits out of the expected range, 
# sometimes, those GESIS codes should be corrected 
s1_gesis_code_corrections_raw_xlsx <- str_subset(s0_pipeline_inputs_raw_chr, "CSB1 CSB2 PUBLIC PRIVATE.xlsx")
s1_gesis_code_corrections_df <- read_xlsx(s1_gesis_code_corrections_raw_xlsx) |>
  filter(!is.na(`NEW CODE`) & `NEW CODE` != "NEW CODE") %>% 
  setNames(c("old_code", "correct_code", "uid", "name", "status", "note")) %>% 
  unique()
# make the adjustment to the mapping file
s1_gesis_xwalk_corrected_df <- s1_gesis_xwalk_filtered_df %>%
  left_join(s1_gesis_code_corrections_df %>% select(code_fs = old_code, correct_code),
            by = c("code_fs")) %>% 
  mutate(code_fs = ifelse(is.na(correct_code), code_fs, correct_code)) %>% 
  select(-correct_code) %>%
  #manually fill the UID from other years for 630151027
  mutate(fs_uid = ifelse(code_fs == "630151027" & grepl("Ankilivalo", FS), 
                         "ZX5EkF6eC0x", 
                         fs_uid)) 








Tip Procedure: Stage 4 — Fill Missing UIDs From The Reviewed Workbook



This stage imports reviewed UID fills and applies them by GESIS clinic code.
#| format: file
# 4) fill in missing UIDs for GESIS-years in mapping ----
# for GESIS-years for public clinics in the mapping file
# reporting data in 2018/2019 using this file for those 4 clinics 
s1_gesis_uid_fills_raw_xlsx <- str_subset(s0_pipeline_inputs_raw_chr, "gesis_missing_uid_in_mapping.xlsx")
s1_gesis_uid_fills_df <- read_xlsx(s1_gesis_uid_fills_raw_xlsx) %>%
  mutate(code_fs = as.character(code_fs))
Join the reviewed fills onto the corrected mapping; leave unrelated UIDs unchanged.
s1_gesis_xwalk_uid_filled_df <- s1_gesis_xwalk_corrected_df %>%
  left_join(s1_gesis_uid_fills_df %>% select(code_fs, uid),
            by = "code_fs") %>% 
  mutate(fs_uid = ifelse(is.na(uid), fs_uid, uid))  %>% 
  select(-uid)
# no GESIS changes, so only concern for this change is if there are other clinics 
# with the same UID --> only one of the UIDs filled in is otherwise in the 
# mapping file, and it appears to be the same clinics in the mapping 
# in the diagnosis dataset, there's a clinic in that same commune that has data 
# for earlier years that seems like its the same "Antanisoa", but it was private
# BUT the GESIS code for that clinic 120143040 also has another name "CMC Ambararata Est", 
# which seems to correspond to when the commune changes for that clinic 
# this clinic was not captured in our 21 GESIS - UIDs with concerning name changes 
# because it was private over that time span
The target retains the narrative evidence associated with these reviewed exceptions next to the transformation.








Tip Procedure: Stage 5 — Reconcile UID-Years With Multiple GESIS Codes



This stage classifies reviewer notes, retains the original internal diagnostic as an executable check, evaluates external GESIS–UID consequences, and applies deletions and renames.
The selected ZIP member is VERIFIER fs_uid_year_with_multiple_gesis.csv and is comma-delimited, as read by the legacy script. The former Drive underscore filename and semicolon dialect are outside this freeze.
#| format: file
# 5) UID-years with multiple GESIS codes ---- 
s1_gesis_multiple_codes_raw_csv <- str_subset(
  s0_pipeline_inputs_raw_chr,
  "VERIFIER fs_uid_year_with_multiple_gesis\\.csv$"
)
s1_gesis_multiple_codes_reviewed_df <- read_csv(s1_gesis_multiple_codes_raw_csv) %>%
  mutate(change = case_when(grepl("the clinic was moved to the district of mandoto", note) ~ "keep", 
                            note %in% c("Same clinic", "OK", "ok") ~ "keep", 
                            grepl("^rename", note) ~ "rename", 
                            grepl("delete|Delete", note) ~ "delete",
                            TRUE ~ as.character(NA)), 
         code_fs = as.character(code_fs)) 
# started with 36 UID-years with multiple GESIS 
# there are 2 deletions, 16 renames, and 18 cases where its just two codes for the same clinic
# --> 18 UID-years with multiple GESIS at the end
# make the change 
s1_gesis_xwalk_multiple_codes_reconciled_df <- s1_gesis_xwalk_uid_filled_df %>%
  # the UIDs got dropped when we rename, which only matters in one case 
  # whe the row needs to be deleted, so separately add in the delete cases vs rest
  left_join(s1_gesis_multiple_codes_reviewed_df %>%
              filter(change == "delete") %>% 
              select(cAnnee, code_fs, fs_uid, change),
            by = c("cAnnee", "code_fs", "fs_uid")) %>%
  filter(change != "delete" | is.na(change)) %>% 
  select(-change) %>% 
  left_join(s1_gesis_multiple_codes_reviewed_df %>%
              filter(change != "delete") %>% 
              select(cAnnee, code_fs, change,
                     fs_uid_correct = UID,
                     fs_name_correct = `NAME CLINICS`),
            by = c("cAnnee", "code_fs")) %>%
  mutate(fs_uid = case_when(change == "rename" & fs_uid_correct == "No UID" ~ "",
                            change == "rename" ~ fs_uid_correct,
                            TRUE ~ fs_uid),
         FS = case_when(change == "rename" & fs_name_correct != "" ~ fs_name_correct, 
                        TRUE ~ FS)) %>%
  select(-(change:fs_name_correct)) %>%
  verify(nrow(.) == 34810)
# deletes 2 rows, so now down to 34810 








Tip Procedure: Stage 6 — Add Reviewed GESIS Codes Missing From The Mapping



This stage constructs the accepted missing clinic across eight mapping years and appends those rows.
A breaking change that must be noted: we aren’t sure if the following adds 8 rows, or adds row index 8…
#| format: file
# 6) 10 GESIS codes not in the mapping ----
# 8 need to be deleted from diagnosis data, 1 doesn't have a UID, lets add row for the last 1
s1_gesis_uid_additions_raw_csv <- str_subset(
  s0_pipeline_inputs_raw_chr,
  "VERIFIER clinic_codes_in_gesis_but_not_in_mapping.csv"
)
s1_gesis_uid_additions_expanded_df <- read_csv(s1_gesis_uid_additions_raw_csv) %>%
  #filter(NOTE != "DELETE" & uid != "NO UID") %>% 
  filter(!is.na(uid) & str_to_lower(uid) != "no uid") %>%
  cross_join(
    tibble(cAnnee = c("2013", "2015", "OLD GESIS 2015", 
                      "NEW GESIS 2015", "2016", "2017", "2018", "2019"))
  ) %>% 
  transmute(cAnnee, 
            code_reg = NA_integer_, 
            region_uid = NA_character_, 
            region = NA_character_, 
            code_dist = NA_integer_, 
            district_uid = NA_character_, 
            district = NA_character_, 
            code_commune = NA_integer_, 
            commune_uid = NA_character_, 
            commune = NA_character_, 
            code_fs = as.character(clinic_code), 
            fs_uid = as.character(uid), 
            TYPE = str_split_fixed(name, " ", 2)[,1],
            FS = as.character(name)) 
Append those reviewed year records to the reconciled mapping.
s1_gesis_xwalk_uid_added_df <- bind_rows(
  s1_gesis_xwalk_multiple_codes_reconciled_df,
  s1_gesis_uid_additions_expanded_df
) %>%
  verify(nrow(.) == 34818)
# adds 8 rows --> 34818  # this is incorrect, it should add row 8








Tip Procedure: Stage 7a — Apply Reviewed Code Substitutions



This stage contains the remaining UID- and year-specific substitutions, deletions, and additions discovered while integrating the mapping with the diagnosis data.
# 7) some manual changes ---- 
# integrating the mapping with the diagnosis dataset identified these problems with the mapping file
s1_gesis_xwalk_manual_codes_corrected_df <- s1_gesis_xwalk_uid_added_df %>%
  mutate(
    code_fs = case_when(
      fs_uid == "naW8NwTF6iT" & cAnnee == "NEW GESIS 2015"                                   ~ "430351007",
      fs_uid == "C43g5TA5l3j" & grepl("2015", cAnnee)                                        ~ "430351006",
      fs_uid == "hVmE01gCHfg" & cAnnee %in% c(2013:2019, "NEW GESIS 2015", "OLD GESIS 2015") ~ "220441038",
      fs_uid == "i9IyexSemHX"                                                                ~ "220441034",
      fs_uid == "xWIEcSCmwUF" & cAnnee == "2010"                                             ~ "440551024",
      fs_uid == "QxMf9Q2KYxI" & cAnnee == "2010"                                             ~ "440541010",
      TRUE                                                                                   ~ code_fs
    )
  )








Tip Procedure: Stage 7b — Replace The Disputed New-2015 Match



Replace the reviewed GESIS/UID pairing for new-2015 with the corresponding old-2015 clinic record. Keep the source row as the evidence for its attributes.
s1_gesis_xwalk_manual_2015_corrected_df <- s1_gesis_xwalk_manual_codes_corrected_df %>%
  # replace what 340141015 is mapping to in new 2015, easier to delete one row and add another
  {
    rows_to_keep <- filter(
      .,
      !(fs_uid == "H9S6IOY4CKL" &
          code_fs == "340141015" &
          cAnnee == "NEW GESIS 2015")
    )

    replacement_row <- filter(
      .,
      fs_uid == "SnRMbMj7ON9" & cAnnee == "OLD GESIS 2015"
    ) %>%
      mutate(
        cAnnee = "NEW GESIS 2015",
        code_fs = "340141015"
      )

    bind_rows(rows_to_keep, replacement_row)
  }








Tip Procedure: Stage 7c — Replace The Historical Match



Construct replacement rows for 2011 through old-2015 from the reviewed 2016 record. The replacement years remain explicit so the affected coverage can be inspected in the checks.
s1_gesis_xwalk_manual_historical_corrected_df <- s1_gesis_xwalk_manual_2015_corrected_df %>%
  # similarly, replace what 520551034 is mapping to in 2011 - old 2015
  {
    replacement_years <- tibble(
      cAnnee = c(2011:2014, "OLD GESIS 2015")
    )

    rows_to_keep <- filter(
      .,
      !(fs_uid == "JnmokyKVSvS" &
          code_fs == "520551034" &
          cAnnee %in% replacement_years$cAnnee)
    )

    replacement_rows <- filter(
      .,
      fs_uid == "d0n2W7psb6s" & cAnnee == "2016"
    ) %>%
      mutate(code_fs = "520551034") %>%
      select(-cAnnee) %>%
      cross_join(replacement_years)

    bind_rows(rows_to_keep, replacement_rows)
  }








Tip Procedure: Stage 7d — Add The Reviewed New-2015 Record



Copy the accepted old-2015 record into new-2015 and assign its reviewed code. Then apply the final UID/year deletions to produce the cleaned mapping.
s1_gesis_xwalk_manual_uid_added_df <- s1_gesis_xwalk_manual_historical_corrected_df %>%
  # add row for "H9S6IOY4CKL" in new 2015  
  {
    existing_rows <- .

    additional_row <- filter(
      .,
      fs_uid == "H9S6IOY4CKL" & cAnnee == "OLD GESIS 2015"
    ) %>%
      mutate(
        cAnnee = "NEW GESIS 2015",
        code_fs = "340141014"
      )

    bind_rows(existing_rows, additional_row)
  }
The final target removes the three excluded UID-years and retains the reviewed row-count assertion.
s1_gesis_xwalk_clean_df <- s1_gesis_xwalk_manual_uid_added_df %>%
  # drop rows for UID noCoZFMcMVa in 2010, 2011, old 2015
  filter(!(fs_uid == "noCoZFMcMVa" & cAnnee %in% c(2010, 2011, "OLD GESIS 2015"))) %>%
  verify(nrow(.) == 34816)
  # nrow # reduces from 34819 to 34816 rows








Warning Check: Compare Most Recent Archived Data And Target Facility Mappings



Review note (2026-11-08). The researcher reports that the initial shape checks on pages 18–21 appear to pass. This records the initial facility-mapping shape review. This is a researcher-reported observation from the interactive review, not an independently rerun acceptance test. It does not establish key-level equality, measurement-value parity, or unchanged diagnosis definitions/IDs. Retain any remaining discrepancies for review.
Run these chunks in order from the repository root after the targets build. These are exploratory summaries; interpretation is left to the reader. Most recent archived data baseline records the selected iterations, evidence, and provenance limits. The shared selection is versioned in src/archived-comparison-baseline.R.
Use the May 1, 2025 script-1 intermediate: the most recent archived data found for this stage.
Load the pair for this page. Braces keep these session assignments out of tar_tangle(); the objects remain available for interactive exploration.
{
  archived_baseline <- dget(here::here("src", "archived-comparison-baseline.R"))
  legacy_zip <- here::here(archived_baseline$archive_zip)
  old_mapping <- read.csv(unz(
    legacy_zip, archived_baseline$facility_mapping_member
  ), check.names = FALSE)
  new_mapping <- targets::tar_read(s1_gesis_xwalk_clean_df)
}
Rows and columns.
tibble::tibble(
  source = c("most recent archived data", "current pipeline"),
  rows = c(nrow(old_mapping), nrow(new_mapping)),
  columns = c(ncol(old_mapping), ncol(new_mapping))
)
Column names and order.
dplyr::bind_rows(
  `most recent archived data` = tibble::tibble(position = seq_len(ncol(old_mapping)), column = names(old_mapping)),
  `current pipeline` = tibble::tibble(position = seq_len(ncol(new_mapping)), column = names(new_mapping)),
  .id = "source"
)
UID coverage by year, including blank or missing UIDs.
dplyr::bind_rows(
  `most recent archived data` = old_mapping |> dplyr::summarise(
    rows = dplyr::n(), uids = dplyr::n_distinct(fs_uid, na.rm = TRUE),
    missing_uids = sum(is.na(fs_uid) | fs_uid == ""), .by = cAnnee
  ),
  `current pipeline` = new_mapping |> dplyr::summarise(
    rows = dplyr::n(), uids = dplyr::n_distinct(fs_uid, na.rm = TRUE),
    missing_uids = sum(is.na(fs_uid) | fs_uid == ""), .by = cAnnee
  ),
  .id = "source"
)

title: 19  Construct Clinic IDs
20  Construct the Diagnosis Dictionary
text:
This page implements 3_construct_dictionary.R as successive targets. It preserves the reviewed cross-wave mappings, supplemental diagnoses, wording corrections, and 40 output-file groups. Wave 3 measurements stay in Parquet: this stage needs their ordered column schema, not their rows.
Translations come from the archived source translations and the bilingual data/clean/diagnosis_dictionary_translated.csv snapshot in the staged ZIP. That snapshot supplies language lookups only; its variable IDs and mapping expressions do not replace the newly constructed dictionary. No translation service is called.






Important Prerequisite: Confirm The Upstream Artifacts



Page 18 must have produced s0_clinic_RMA_W3_clean_parquet, and page 20 must have selected s2_clinic_months_raw_zip. In an authorized R session, confirm that these tracked files exist. This check reads target metadata and paths, not the measurement tables.
stopifnot(
  all(file.exists(targets::tar_read(s0_clinic_RMA_W3_clean_parquet))),
  all(file.exists(targets::tar_read(s2_clinic_months_raw_zip)))
)
Authoring remains globally unevaluated. The helpers below are declared in procedures because tar_tangle() also tracks top-level function assignments. The procedure declarations are wired into the graph by the execution page.








Tip Procedure: Declare Archive And Text Helpers



Resolve exact archive-member suffixes and extract only the selected input into a temporary directory. Each reader must return a materialized small object before extraction cleanup; no temporary path becomes a downstream input.
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(stringr)
library(readr)
library(readxl)
library(duckplyr)
library(targets)

s3_dictionary_archive_member_fn <- function(archive, suffix) {
  members <- utils::unzip(archive, list = TRUE)$Name
  hits <- members[endsWith(members, paste0("/", suffix)) &
                    !grepl("(^|/)__MACOSX/", members)]
  if (length(hits) != 1L) stop("Expected one archive member for: ", suffix)
  unname(hits)
}
s3_dictionary_archive_read_fn <- function(archive, member, reader) {
  stopifnot(length(member) == 1L, !grepl("^/|(^|/)\\.\\.(/|$)", member))
  extraction_dir <- tempfile("dictionary-input-")
  dir.create(extraction_dir)
  on.exit(unlink(extraction_dir, recursive = TRUE), add = TRUE)
  path <- utils::unzip(archive, files = member, exdir = extraction_dir)
  stopifnot(length(path) == 1L, file.exists(path))
  reader(path)
}

s3_dictionary_read_csv_fn <- function(archive, member) {
  s3_dictionary_archive_read_fn(archive, member, function(path) {
    read.csv(path, fileEncoding = "UTF-8", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  })
}
Apply the legacy wording substitutions sequentially. Unequal non-scalar pattern/replacement vectors fail explicitly instead of calling the legacy undefined error() function.
s3_diagnosis_multiple_gsub_fn <- function(patterns, replacements, x) {
  if (length(patterns) != length(replacements) &&
      length(patterns) != 1L && length(replacements) != 1L) {
    stop("Pattern and replacement must have equal length or be scalar.")
  }
  count <- max(length(patterns), length(replacements))
  patterns <- rep_len(patterns, count)
  replacements <- rep_len(replacements, count)
  for (i in seq_len(count)) x <- gsub(patterns[[i]], replacements[[i]], x)
  x
}








Tip Procedure: Select The Dictionary Sources



The staged ZIP is already a file target. Member names below are selectors inside that tracked archive, not independent filesystem paths. Select the current data/raw versions explicitly so the parallel review and OLD copies cannot be chosen accidentally.
s3_dictionary_archive_members_chr <- {
  suffixes <- c(
    mapping = "data/raw/diagnosis_mapping/diagnosis_mapping_updated_1march2024_withspecialchar_fixw3b.csv",
    wave12 = "data/raw/diagnosis_mapping/Big Dictionary Revised_with_wave - withID.csv",
    diar_pneu = "data/raw/from_Kevin/mdg_tall_split/diar_pneu_fix.csv",
    additional = "data/raw/from_Kevin/Big Dictionary Revised_v2.xlsx",
    wave3 = "data/raw/diagnosis_mapping/symphonia w3_diagnoses_with_zero_years_MLC_updated_unordered_w3.csv",
    anemia = "data/raw/anemie_2020.csv",
    translations = "data/raw/diagnosis_dictionary_ordered_file_translated.csv",
    archived = "data/clean/diagnosis_dictionary_translated.csv",
    dir1 = "data/raw/from_Kevin/updated_dictionary/dir1_diagnostic_codes.xlsx",
    dir2 = "data/raw/from_Kevin/updated_dictionary/dir2_diagnostic_codes.xlsx"
  )
  vapply(suffixes, function(suffix) {
    s3_dictionary_archive_member_fn(s2_clinic_months_raw_zip, suffix)
  }, character(1))
}








Tip Procedure: Record The Ordered Wave 3 Schema



Read the prepared Parquet column names without collecting measurements. Append only anemia columns absent from that schema, after the legacy ? to ≥ correction and removal of its two descriptive organisation columns. Persist this schema as an ordinary target: downstream measurement cleaning must use these same X identifiers rather than inventing another column order.
s3_w3_anemia_columns_chr <- s3_dictionary_archive_read_fn(
  s2_clinic_months_raw_zip, s3_dictionary_archive_members_chr[["anemia"]],
  function(path) {
    columns <- names(read_csv_duckdb(path, prudence = "stingy"))
    columns <- gsub("?", "≥", columns, fixed = TRUE)
    setdiff(columns, c("organisationunitcode", "organisationunitdescription"))
  }
)

s3_w3_column_dictionary_df <- {
  columns <- names(read_parquet_duckdb(
    s0_clinic_RMA_W3_clean_parquet, prudence = "stingy"
  ))
  bind_rows(
    tibble(w3_description = columns, orig = TRUE),
    tibble(w3_description = setdiff(s3_w3_anemia_columns_chr, columns), orig = FALSE)
  ) |>
    mutate(w3_colname = paste0("X", row_number()))
}
s3_diagnosis_mapping_source_df <- s3_dictionary_read_csv_fn(
  s2_clinic_months_raw_zip, s3_dictionary_archive_members_chr[["mapping"]]
) |>
  select(-wave3_colname_orig, -wave3_colname_noAccent)








Tip Procedure: Tidy The Wave 1–2 Dictionary



Retain the legacy diagnostic-code filter and remove the old Wave 1 diarrhea and pneumonia definitions. read.csv() preserves the legacy syntactic column names, including ID.; changing them here would break the reviewed joins.
s3_diagnosis_wave12_dictionary_df <- s3_dictionary_read_csv_fn(
  s2_clinic_months_raw_zip, s3_dictionary_archive_members_chr[["wave12"]]
) |>
  filter(Diagnostic.Code..cCode. != "") |>
  filter(!(Diagnostic.Code..cCode. %in% c("Diarrhea", "Pneumonia") &
             wave == "Wave 1")) |>
  select(-Column.Type)








Tip Procedure: Read Replacement Diarrhea And Pneumonia Definitions



Reduce the replacement tall CSV in DuckDB to distinct cCode/Variable pairs. Preserve first-occurrence order before collecting those definitions; this order contributes to subsequent variable numbering. The measurement values are never collected into R.
s3_diagnosis_diar_pneu_variables_df <- s3_dictionary_archive_read_fn(

Tip Procedure: Aggregate Comparable Variables Across Waves



The shared reducer retains the legacy missing-component rule: if one component is unmatched, the aggregate for that other wave is missing. Repeated source expressions are cleared before retaining the first complete expression combination. These rules affect comparability and are not replaced by a generic sum or coalesce.
Select local column names with all_of()/pick() when the helper runs. This preserves grouped column lookup while avoiding premature unquotation when tar_tangle() declares the function target.
s3_diagnosis_aggregate_to_wave_fn <- function(df, target_wave,
                                     all_waves = paste0("wave", c(1:2, "3A", "3B"))) {
  other_waves = setdiff(all_waves, target_wave)
  target_col = paste0(target_wave, "_colname")
  target_desc = paste0(target_wave, "_description")
  other_col = paste0(other_waves, "_colname")
  filter(df, if_any(all_of(target_col), ~ !is.na(.x))) %>%
    summarise(description = unique(pick(all_of(target_desc))[[1L]]),
              across(all_of(other_col),
                     ~if(any(is.na(.x))){NA}else{paste(unique(.x), collapse = " + ")}),
              .by = all_of(target_col)) %>%
    mutate(wave1_colname = ifelse(n() == 1, wave1_colname, NA),
           .by = c(wave1_colname)) %>%
    mutate(wave2_colname = ifelse(n() == 1, wave2_colname, NA),
           .by = c(wave2_colname)) %>%
    mutate(wave3A_colname = ifelse(n() == 1, wave3A_colname, NA),
           .by = c(wave3A_colname)) %>%
    mutate(wave3B_colname = ifelse(n() == 1, wave3B_colname, NA),
           .by = c(wave3B_colname)) %>%
    return
}

Tip Procedure: Declare Validation And Artifact Inspection Helpers



Validate the source-expression contract without evaluating expressions as R code. Report reused complete expressions, repeated summands, and terms absent from the corresponding source schema. Missing expressions remain allowed; they indicate that a comparable definition is unavailable in that wave.
s3_diagnosis_validate_fn <- function(dictionary, wave3_schema, wave12_dictionary) {
  empty <- tibble(var = character(), wave = character(), issue = character(),
                  expression = character())
  issues <- list(empty)
  for (wave in c("wave1", "wave2", "wave3A", "wave3B")) {
    expressions <- dictionary[[paste0(wave, "_colname")]]
    columns <- if (wave %in% c("wave1", "wave2")) {
      wave12_dictionary$Column.Name
    } else wave3_schema$w3_colname
    reused <- duplicated(expressions) | duplicated(expressions, fromLast = TRUE)
    for (i in which(!is.na(expressions))) {
      terms <- strsplit(expressions[[i]], " + ", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
      problems <- c(if (reused[[i]]) "reused_expression",
                    if (anyDuplicated(terms)) "repeated_summand",
                    if (any(!terms %in% columns)) "unknown_source_column")
      if (length(problems)) issues[[length(issues) + 1L]] <- tibble(
        var = dictionary$var[[i]], wave = wave,
        issue = problems, expression = expressions[[i]]
      )
    }
  }
  bind_rows(issues)
}
The artifact inspector asks DuckDB for a scalar count and reads the file size from filesystem metadata. It never collects the dictionary rows, or the upstream Wave 3 measurement table.
s3_diagnosis_parquet_stats_fn <- function(path) {
  stopifnot(length(path) == 1L, file.exists(path))
  relation <- read_parquet_duckdb(path, prudence = "stingy")
  counts <- relation |> summarise(rows = n()) |> collect()
  tibble(file = basename(path), bytes = unname(file.info(path)$size),
         rows = counts$rows, columns = length(names(relation)))
}

title: 22  Reconcile Sectorization and Construct Healthsheds
text:
This page implements pinned legacy stage 5 at 31e0769683e133e136b09ac0c6608c5a12657a9a. Each reviewed correction round is a separate target. Shared FKT assignments, population accounting, missing-value behavior, join multiplicity, and residual non-contiguity retain legacy rules. Spatial handoffs are ordinary sf targets; nonspatial exports use Parquet. The execution page tangles these declarations without executing scientific code during rendering.






Important Prerequisite: Require The Reviewed Inputs And Spatial Runtime



Require the tracked s2_clinic_months_raw_zip and s1_gesis_xwalk_clean_df, the rebuilt native runtime, and the package acceptance checks. All stage-5 inputs below are exact data/raw/ members of that tracked archive; the similarly named from Symphonia/ sectorization copy is not substituted. The complete shapefile bundle is extracted privately and read before cleanup. No raw source or reviewed decision is edited.








Tip Procedure: Declare Archive, Geometry, And Matching Helpers



Helpers are tracked function targets, not an unresolved source() call. The grouped fuzzy join preserves original row identifiers, shared-group boundaries, cosine distance, callback selection, and ties. The topology helper uses the legacy DE-9IM positions 1, 2, 4, and 5; point contact alone does not connect polygons. Relation matrices are decoded directly in R, avoiding a data-frame mutation for every clinic. Population summation likewise uses base-R pair deduplication: attaching duckplyr replaces unique.data.frame(), which would otherwise execute a DuckDB query for each clinic group. As in the legacy script, st_relate() uses planar DE-9IM on the source longitude/latitude coordinates; its repeated informational notice is suppressed, while errors and warnings propagate. Empty healthsheds are constructed with the input CRS.
s5_healthshed_drop_geometry_fn <- function(x) {
  x <- as.data.frame(x)
  x[!vapply(x, inherits, logical(1), what = "sfc")]
}
s5_healthshed_runtime_fn <- function() {
  packages <- c("sf", "s2", "units", "igraph", "fuzzyjoin", "stringdist", "dplyr")
  list(R = as.character(getRversion()),
       packages = setNames(vapply(packages, function(x) as.character(utils::packageVersion(x)), character(1)), packages),
       engines = sf::sf_extSoftVersion(), s2 = sf::sf_use_s2(),
       native_lock_md5 = if (file.exists("/opt/spack-environment/spack.lock"))
         unname(tools::md5sum("/opt/spack-environment/spack.lock")) else NA_character_)
}
s5_healthshed_read_fn <- function(archive, members, name, kind = "csv", colClasses = NULL, ...) {
  s3_dictionary_archive_read_fn(archive, members[[name]], function(path) {
    if (kind == "xlsx") return(readxl::read_excel(path, ...))
    if (kind == "rds") return(readRDS(path))
    columns <- names(read.csv(path, nrows = 0L, fileEncoding = "UTF-8"))
    ids <- columns[grepl("uid|instat|code|pcode", columns, ignore.case = TRUE)]
    if (is.null(colClasses)) colClasses <- setNames(rep("character", length(ids)), ids)
    read.csv(path, colClasses = colClasses,
             fileEncoding = "UTF-8", stringsAsFactors = FALSE, ...)
  })
}
s5_healthshed_shapes_read_fn <- function(archive, members) {
  unsafe <- startsWith(members, "/") | vapply(strsplit(members, "/", fixed = TRUE), function(x) any(x == ".."), logical(1))
  stopifnot(length(members) >= 4L, !any(unsafe))
  required <- c("shp", "shx", "dbf", "prj")
  stopifnot(all(required %in% tools::file_ext(members)))
  scratch <- tempfile("healthshed-shapes-")
  dir.create(scratch)
  on.exit(unlink(scratch, recursive = TRUE), add = TRUE)
  paths <- utils::unzip(archive, files = members, exdir = scratch)
  stopifnot(all(file.exists(paths)))
  sf::read_sf(paths[endsWith(paths, ".shp")])
}
s5_healthshed_adjacency_fn <- function(x, y = x) {
  # st_relate uses planar DE-9IM even for geographic coordinates, as in stage 5.
  relation <- suppressMessages(sf::st_relate(x, y))
  matrix(grepl("1|2", paste0(substr(relation, 1, 2), substr(relation, 4, 5))),
         nrow = length(x), ncol = length(y))
}
s5_healthshed_components_fn <- function(x) {
  if (!length(x)) return(0L)
  igraph::components(igraph::graph_from_adjacency_matrix(s5_healthshed_adjacency_fn(x)), mode = "weak")$no
}
s5_grouped_stringdist_fulljoin_fn <- function(df1, df2, df1_group, df2_group,
    df1_stringmatch, df2_stringmatch, dist_method = "cosine", dist_col = "dist",
    max_dist = 30, ignore_case = TRUE, select_match = identity, unnest = TRUE, ...) {
  left <- as.data.frame(df1) %>% mutate(df1_id = seq_len(n())) %>% nest_by(across(all_of(df1_group)), .key = "df1")
  right <- as.data.frame(df2) %>% mutate(df2_id = seq_len(n())) %>% nest_by(across(all_of(df2_group)), .key = "df2")
  # Legacy full_join + removal of absent nested groups keeps shared groups only.
  joined <- inner_join(left, right, by = setNames(df2_group, df1_group)) %>%
    rowwise() %>% mutate(df_new = list(select_match(fuzzyjoin::stringdist_join(
      df1, df2, by = setNames(df2_stringmatch, df1_stringmatch), mode = "full",
      method = dist_method, distance_col = dist_col, max_dist = max_dist,
      ignore_case = ignore_case, ...))))
  if (unnest) joined <- joined %>% select(-df1, -df2) %>% tidyr::unnest(df_new)
  joined
}
s5_healthshed_refresh_fn <- function(x, lookup, shapes, fallback = FALSE) {
  x <- s5_healthshed_drop_geometry_fn(x)
  previous <- if (fallback && "ADM4_PCODE" %in% names(x)) x$ADM4_PCODE else rep(NA_character_, nrow(x))
  x$ADM4_PCODE <- NULL
  x$.s5_previous_pcode <- previous
  x <- left_join(x, select(lookup, ADM4C_BNGRC, ADM4_PCODE), by = c("fkt_instat_clean" = "ADM4C_BNGRC"))
  if (fallback) x$ADM4_PCODE <- coalesce(x$ADM4_PCODE, x$.s5_previous_pcode)
  x$.s5_previous_pcode <- NULL
  x <- left_join(x, as.data.frame(select(shapes, ADM4_PCODE)), by = "ADM4_PCODE")
  sf::st_as_sf(x)
}
s5_healthshed_aggregate_fn <- function(sect_df){
  empty_geom <- sf::st_sfc(sf::st_geometrycollection(), crs = sf::st_crs(sect_df))
  sect_df %>%
    filter(!(is.na(fkt_uid) | fkt_uid == "" | is.na(fkt_name) | fkt_name == "")) %>% #pull(fs_uid) %>% n_distinct()
    sf::st_as_sf() %>%
    group_by(fs_uid) %>%
    # for each clinic, merge the shapefiles
    summarise(# since some fkt_uid get matched twice, have to take only unique ones
      # before summing the population
      fs_pop = sum(fkt_pop_2022[!duplicated(data.frame(
        fkt_uid = fkt_uid, fkt_pop_2022 = fkt_pop_2022))], na.rm = TRUE),
      n_fkt_uid = n_distinct(fkt_uid, na.rm = T),
      n_fkt_instat = n_distinct(fkt_instat_clean, na.rm = T),
      across(c(region_uid:district_name,
               starts_with("fs"),
               n_fkt_instat, n_fkt_uid),
             function(x){unique(na.omit(x))}),
      # recalculate the number of components
      n_components = {if(n_distinct(fkt_instat_clean, na.rm = T) > 0){
        s5_healthshed_components_fn(geometry[!is.na(fkt_instat_clean)])} else{0}},
              geometry = {if(n_distinct(fkt_instat_clean, na.rm = T) > 0){
                sf::st_union(geometry[!is.na(fkt_instat_clean)]) %>%
                  sf::st_combine() %>%
                  sf::st_make_valid()} else {empty_geom}}) %>%
    rowwise() %>%
    mutate(n_shape = length(geometry[[1]])) %>%
    ungroup
}








Tip Procedure: Select Exact Archived Sources And Record The Geometry Environment



The execution page records s5_spatial_runtime_list with an always-check cue. Its unchanged value lets downstream targets skip; changed package, engine, or topology settings invalidate the spatial read. It does not change the global s2 setting or projection.
s5_healthshed_archive_members_list <- {
  suffixes <- c(
    lookup = "data/raw/bngrc_codes_lut_pcodes_2018.xlsx",
    sectorization = "data/raw/mapping GESIS DHIS questions - FKT code instat.csv",
    duplicates = "data/raw/symphonia_verified/VERIFIER duplicated_fkt_instat_in_sectorisation2022.csv",
    match1 = "data/raw/symphonia_verified/VERIFIER fkt_name_matching_for_sectorisation2022.csv",
    manual1 = "data/raw/symphonia_verified/FKT SECTO UNMATCHED.xlsx",
    manual2 = "data/raw/geolocation/manual_fkt_match.csv",
    match2 = "data/raw/symphonia_verified/VERIFIER fkt_name_matching_for_sectorisation2022_v2.csv",
    match3 = "data/raw/symphonia_verified/VERIFIER fkt_name_matching_for_sectorisation2022_v3.csv",
    sectorization2018 = "data/raw/sectorisation 2018.xlsx",
    manual3 = "data/raw/geolocation/manual_fkt_match_v2.csv",
    manual4 = "data/raw/geolocation/manual_fkt_match_v3.csv",
    unmatch = "data/raw/geolocation/unmatch_fkt.csv",
    districts = "data/raw/geolocation/sect_ocha_district_match.rds",
    final_reviews = "data/raw/from Symphonia/Verification secto vs ocha.xlsx",
    reassignments = "data/raw/symphonia_verified/noncontig_v2_fix.csv")
  tables <- vapply(suffixes, function(suffix) s3_dictionary_archive_member_fn(s2_clinic_months_raw_zip, suffix), character(1))
  names <- utils::unzip(s2_clinic_months_raw_zip, list = TRUE)$Name
  stem <- "data/raw/mdg_adm_bngrc_ocha_20181031_shp/mdg_admbnda_adm4_BNGRC_OCHA_20181031."
  shapes <- names[grepl(stem, names, fixed = TRUE) & !grepl("(^|/)__MACOSX/", names)]
  stopifnot(length(shapes) > 0L, !anyDuplicated(basename(shapes)))
  list(tables = tables, shapes = shapes)
}
s5_fkt_shapes_source_sf <- {
  s5_spatial_runtime_list
  s5_healthshed_shapes_read_fn(s2_clinic_months_raw_zip, s5_healthshed_archive_members_list$shapes)
}
s5_fkt_shapes_valid_sf <- sf::st_make_valid(s5_fkt_shapes_source_sf)








Tip Procedure: Split Nosy Mitsio And Reconcile Population



The initial split retains the source’s first-polygon versus remaining-parts rule. Part order, bounds, areas, source CRS, and library versions are recorded in the split audit. A synthetic test makes the order dependency explicit. Population merging uses the reviewed notes and the source’s sum/NA semantics; shared assignments are not deduplicated across clinics.
s5_fkt_shapes_initial_sf <- {
  fkt_shape <- s5_fkt_shapes_valid_sf
  # Pinned stage 5, lines 61–74.
  fkt_shape <- rbind(fkt_shape %>%
                       filter(ADM4_PCODE != "MG71717150005"),
                     fkt_shape %>%
                       filter(ADM4_PCODE == "MG71717150005") %>%
                       sf::st_cast("POLYGON") %>%
                       mutate(group = (seq_len(n())) > 1) %>%
                       summarise(across(!geometry, unique),
                                 geometry = sf::st_union(geometry),
                                 .by = group) %>%
                       select(-group) %>%
                       mutate(ADM4_EN = ifelse(seq_len(n()) == 1,
                                               ADM4_EN,
                                               "Nosy Mitsio"),
                              ADM4_PCODE = paste0(ADM4_PCODE, LETTERS[seq_len(n())])))
  fkt_shape
}
s5_fkt_code_lookup_source_df <- s5_healthshed_read_fn(
  s2_clinic_months_raw_zip, s5_healthshed_archive_members_list$tables, "lookup", "xlsx", sheet = 5) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), as.character))
s5_fkt_code_lookup_initial_df <- {
  ocha_map <- s5_fkt_code_lookup_source_df
  # Pinned stage 5, lines 80–88.
  ocha_map <- ocha_map %>%
    {rbind(filter(., ADM4_PCODE != "MG71717150005"),
           filter(., ADM4_PCODE == "MG71717150005") %>%
             mutate(across(c(ADM4_PCODE, ADM4C_BNGRC),
                           ~paste0(.x, "A"))),
           filter(., ADM4_PCODE == "MG71717150005") %>%
             mutate(across(c(ADM4_PCODE, ADM4C_BNGRC),
                           ~paste0(.x, "B")),
                    ADM4_EN = "Nosy Mitsio",
                    ADM4E_BNGRC = "NOSY MITSIO"))}
  ocha_map
}
s5_sectorization_2022_source_df <- {
  x <- s5_healthshed_read_fn(s2_clinic_months_raw_zip, s5_healthshed_archive_members_list$tables, "sectorization", colClasses = "character")
  stopifnot(ncol(x) == 17L)
  names(x) <- c("region_uid", "region_name", "district_uid", "district_name", "commune_uid", "commune_name",
                "fs_uid", "fs_type", "fs_name", "f_or_nf", "geometry", "fkt_uid", "fkt_instat", "fkt_name",
                "fkt_pop_2022", "distance_csb_fkt", "transit")
  x[c("fkt_pop_2022", "distance_csb_fkt", "transit")] <- lapply(x[c("fkt_pop_2022", "distance_csb_fkt", "transit")], type.convert, as.is = TRUE)
  mutate(x, fkt_instat = ifelse(fkt_instat == "717150005", "717150005A", fkt_instat))
}
s5_sectorization_duplicate_reviews_df <- s5_healthshed_read_fn(
  s2_clinic_months_raw_zip, s5_healthshed_archive_members_list$tables, "duplicates")
s5_sectorization_population_reconciled_df <- {
  sect <- s5_sectorization_2022_source_df
  dup_fkt_instat <- s5_sectorization_duplicate_reviews_df
  # Pinned stage 5, lines 111–121.
  sect_filled <- sect %>%
    left_join(dup_fkt_instat %>%
                mutate(fkt_instat = as.character(fkt_instat)) %>%
                select(fkt_uid, fkt_instat, NOTE)) %>%
    group_by(fkt_instat) %>%
    mutate(merge_fkt = any(grepl("keep that row", NOTE)) & any(NOTE == "delete"),
           fkt_pop_2022 = ifelse(merge_fkt, sum(fkt_pop_2022), fkt_pop_2022)) %>%
    ungroup %>%
    filter(!merge_fkt | (merge_fkt & NOTE != "delete")) %>%
    select(-merge_fkt, -NOTE)
  # drops 6 rows --> 21880 to 21874
  sect_filled

Tip Procedure: Split Coastal Islands And Apply The Final Unlinks



The largest polygon remains mainland except for MG71713253004, where the smallest part is separated as in the source. The _A lookup extension and new assignment rows are updated together. The final review first unlinks old clinic assignments, appends the new rows with missing population, and then refreshes geometry with the legacy old-PCODE fallback.
s5_sectorization_island_assignments_df <- {
  ocha_map <- s5_fkt_code_lookup_initial_df
  # Pinned stage 5, lines 666–672.
  island_fixes <- data.frame(fkt_instat = c("713151001", "713151004",
                                            "713232005", "713254003",
                                            "713253004", "713010004"),
                             fs_uid = c("Z0mzcQCqySd", "Z0mzcQCqySd",
                                        "Zmgnljl5frE", "yPSYALQxVv2",
                                        "yPSYALQxVv2", "wnWoQcrvINJ")) %>%
    left_join(ocha_map %>% select(fkt_instat = ADM4C_BNGRC, ADM4_PCODE))
  island_fixes
}
The coastal split retains the literal legacy expression: area ranks are computed per feature, while the special-code comparison uses the maximum rank across the six features. In the archived inputs, that feature has three parts and the global maximum rank is three. This distinction matters if the source geometry is replaced; the split audit records each part explicitly.
s5_fkt_shapes_final_sf <- {
  fkt_shape <- s5_fkt_shapes_initial_sf
  island_fixes <- s5_sectorization_island_assignments_df
  # Pinned stage 5, lines 674–700.
  fkt_shape <- rbind(fkt_shape %>%
                       filter(ADM4_PCODE %in% c(island_fixes$ADM4_PCODE) == FALSE),
                     fkt_shape %>%
                       filter(ADM4_PCODE %in% c(island_fixes$ADM4_PCODE)) %>%
                       mutate(row_id = seq_len(n())) %>%
                       sf::st_cast("POLYGON") %>%
                       mutate(area = sf::st_area(geometry)) %>%
                       mutate(area_rank = rank(-area), # biggest is rank 1, smallest is max rank
                              .by = row_id) %>%
                       # for groups 1-3, 5 the largest shape is mainland and other islands can go together
                       # for group 4, smallest island goes separate, larger island can stay with mainland
                       # for 5, i think the land is bigger, its the second element when its cast
                       mutate(mainland = ifelse(ADM4_PCODE != "MG71713253004", area_rank == 1, area_rank != max(area_rank))) %>%
                       select(-starts_with("area")) %>%
                       # merge the mainland and non-mainland pieces
                       summarise(across(!geometry, unique),
                                 geometry = sf::st_union(geometry),
                                 .by = c(row_id, mainland)) %>%
                       select(-row_id) %>%
                       # if its the mainland, leave the name and pcode, if its non-mainlan, add a letter to the name and pcode
                       mutate(ADM4_EN = ifelse(mainland,
                                               ADM4_EN,
                                               paste0(ADM4_EN, "_A")),
                              ADM4_PCODE = ifelse(mainland,
                                                  ADM4_PCODE,
                                                  paste0(ADM4_PCODE, "_A"))) %>%
                       select(-mainland))
  fkt_shape
}
s5_fkt_code_lookup_final_df <- {
  ocha_map <- s5_fkt_code_lookup_initial_df
  island_fixes <- s5_sectorization_island_assignments_df
  # Pinned stage 5, lines 702–705.
  ocha_map <- ocha_map %>% rbind(ocha_map %>%
                        filter(ADM4C_BNGRC %in% island_fixes$fkt_instat) %>%
                        mutate(across(starts_with("ADM4"), ~paste0(.x, "_A"))))
  ocha_map
}
s5_sectorization_islands_fixed_sf <- {
  sect_filled_v4 <- as.data.frame(s5_sectorization_misc_fixed_sf)

    full_join(island_fixes %>% select(-ADM4_PCODE) %>%
                mutate(fkt_instat_clean = paste0(fkt_instat, "_A"),
                       fkt_uid = "none",
                       fkt_name = "-",
                       match_type = "island_fix") %>%
                select(-fkt_instat) %>%
                # add the fs info from the sect file
                left_join(sect_filled_v4 %>%
                            filter(!is.na(f_or_nf)) %>%
                            select(region_uid:fs_ll) %>%
                            distinct))

  s5_healthshed_refresh_fn(sect_filled_v4, s5_fkt_code_lookup_final_df, s5_fkt_shapes_final_sf)

s5_sectorization_final_reassignment_reviews_df <- s5_healthshed_read_fn(
  s2_clinic_months_raw_zip, s5_healthshed_archive_members_list$tables, "reassignments") %>%

              by = c("fkt_instat_clean" = "ADM4C_BNGRC")) %>%
    left_join(noncontig_fixes2 %>% transmute(ADM4_PCODE, old_fs_uid, unmatch = T),
              by = c("ADM4_PCODE", "fs_uid" = "old_fs_uid")) %>%

s5_sectorization_final_reassignment_rows_df <- {
