Tip Procedure: Retain Audits And Review Plots Without Publishing Protected Data



The audit reports coverage and population at every major round. Historical counts are comparison observations, not universal assertions. Plot-list targets contain clinic diagnostics for authorized review and are never rendered into this manual. True polygon-part counts are audited separately from the literal legacy n_shape field.
s5_healthshed_audit_fn <- function(sectorizations, shapes) {
  bind_rows(lapply(names(sectorizations), function(round) {
    x <- sectorizations[[round]]
    tibble::tibble(round = round, rows = nrow(x), clinics = n_distinct(x$fs_uid, na.rm = TRUE),
      population = sum(x$fkt_pop_2022, na.rm = TRUE),
      unmatched_assignment_rows = sum(is.na(x$fkt_instat_clean)),
      unmatched_polygons = sum(!shapes$ADM4_PCODE %in% x$ADM4_PCODE),
      empty_assignment_geometries = sum(sf::st_is_empty(x)),
      unknown_pcodes = sum(!is.na(x$ADM4_PCODE) & !x$ADM4_PCODE %in% shapes$ADM4_PCODE))
  }))
}
s5_healthshed_assignment_audit_df <- s5_healthshed_audit_fn(list(
  initial = s5_sectorization_contiguity_filtered_sf, v2 = s5_sectorization_reviewed_v2_sf,
  v3 = s5_sectorization_commune_filled_sf, final = s5_sectorization_2022_clean_sf), s5_fkt_shapes_final_sf)
s5_healthshed_clinic_audit_df <- s5_healthshed_clinic_final_sf %>%
  mutate(polygon_parts = lengths(sf::st_geometry(s5_healthshed_clinic_final_sf)),
         empty_geometry = sf::st_is_empty(s5_healthshed_clinic_final_sf)) %>% sf::st_drop_geometry()
s5_fkt_split_audit_df <- bind_rows(lapply(c("source", "initial", "final"), function(stage) {
  x <- switch(stage, source = s5_fkt_shapes_valid_sf, initial = s5_fkt_shapes_initial_sf, final = s5_fkt_shapes_final_sf)
  split_codes <- c("MG71717150005", s5_sectorization_island_assignments_df$ADM4_PCODE)
  selected <- x %>% filter(sub("(_A|[AB])$", "", ADM4_PCODE) %in% split_codes)
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(selected)), function(i) {
    parts <- suppressWarnings(sf::st_cast(sf::st_geometry(selected[i, ]), "POLYGON"))
    bounds <- t(vapply(parts, function(part) sf::st_bbox(part), numeric(4)))
    tibble::tibble(stage = stage, ADM4_PCODE = selected$ADM4_PCODE[[i]], part = seq_along(parts),
      area_m2 = as.numeric(sf::st_area(parts)), xmin = bounds[,1], ymin = bounds[,2],
      xmax = bounds[,3], ymax = bounds[,4], wkt = sf::st_as_text(parts), crs_wkt = sf::st_crs(x)$wkt)
  }))
}))
s5_healthshed_review_plots_fn <- function(sheds, assignments, multipart = FALSE) {
  selected <- if (multipart) filter(sheds, n_components == 1, n_shape > 1) else filter(sheds, n_components > 1)
  plots <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(selected)), function(i) {
    focus <- selected[i, ]
    nearby <- sf::st_filter(sheds, sf::st_as_sfc(sf::st_bbox(focus)))
    cells <- filter(assignments, fs_uid %in% nearby$fs_uid)
    plot <- ggplot2::ggplot() + ggplot2::geom_sf(data = nearby, ggplot2::aes(fill = fs_uid)) +
      ggplot2::geom_sf(data = cells, fill = NA, colour = "grey35", linetype = "dotted") +
      ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = MetBrewer::met.brewer("Renoir", nrow(nearby))) +
      ggplot2::ggtitle(paste(focus$fs_uid, focus$fs_name, focus$district_name, sep = ": ")) +
      ggplot2::coord_sf(xlim = extendrange(sf::st_bbox(focus)[c(1, 3)], f = 0.5),
                        ylim = extendrange(sf::st_bbox(focus)[c(2, 4)], f = 0.5)) + ggplot2::theme_void()
    locations <- sf::st_drop_geometry(nearby) %>%
      filter(!is.na(fs_ll), grepl("^POINT[[:space:]]*[(]", fs_ll))
    if (nrow(locations)) {
      locations <- sf::st_sf(locations, geometry = sf::st_as_sfc(locations$fs_ll, crs = sf::st_crs(sheds)))
      plot <- plot + ggplot2::geom_sf(data = locations, colour = "grey15", size = 2, inherit.aes = FALSE)
    }
    plot
  })
  setNames(plots, selected$fs_uid)
}
s5_healthshed_clinic_noncontiguous_review_list <- s5_healthshed_review_plots_fn(
  s5_healthshed_clinic_final_sf, s5_sectorization_2022_clean_sf)
s5_healthshed_clinic_multipart_review_list <- s5_healthshed_review_plots_fn(
  s5_healthshed_clinic_final_sf, s5_sectorization_2022_clean_sf, multipart = TRUE)








Tip Procedure: Expose Spatial Handoffs And Nonspatial Parquet Products



Pages 24–25 consume the final sectorization and healthshed sf objects directly, retaining full field names and geometry. Only explicit nonspatial assignment/audit exports are written below. No shapefile field truncation or new spatial interchange format is introduced.
s5_healthshed_write_table_fn <- function(x, path) {
  dir.create(dirname(path), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  duckplyr::compute_parquet(duckplyr::as_duckdb_tibble(as.data.frame(x)), path)
  path
}

# Shape check: healthsheds-dimensions
healthshed_shape <- function(x) {
  valid <- sf::st_is_valid(x)
  tibble::tibble(
    rows = nrow(x), columns = length(names(x)),
    attribute_columns = sum(!vapply(x, inherits, logical(1), what = "sfc")),

    empty_geometries = sum(sf::st_is_empty(x), na.rm = TRUE),
    invalid_geometries = sum(!valid, na.rm = TRUE),
    unknown_validity = sum(is.na(valid))
  )
}

title: 23  Compare and Select Clinic Locations
text:
This page implements 6_locate_clinics.R at pinned revision 31e0769683e133e136b09ac0c6608c5a12657a9a. Each row is a clinic-location candidate, not necessarily a unique clinic. Matching ties and full-join-only clinics remain visible. Five reported coordinate sources, a matched FKT, and a healthshed supply the evidence for the fixed source-selection order. A selected centroid label denotes an inferred location, not a measured point.






Important Prerequisite: Require Identities, Geometry, And Frozen Location Sources



Require s2_clinic_ids_df, s5_sectorization_2022_clean_sf, and s5_healthshed_clinic_final_sf from pages 20 and 23. Read the four exact source members from the tracked s2_clinic_months_raw_zip; do not retrieve current master lists. The GPS source describes FKT centers. Other location files mentioned only in the legacy scratch section are not active inputs.
Reuse the page-23 spatial runtime and page-21 archive extraction helpers. Spatial handoffs retain full field names, including distance_csb_fkt and fkt_instat_clean, instead of reconstructing truncated shapefile names km_fkt and fkt_nst. Raw source tables retain coordinate text and source IDs. Scientific targets run only in the compute-node allocation. Rendering and synthetic checks do not build targets.








Tip Procedure: Declare Source, Point, And Intersection Helpers



unique_nonNA() follows the legacy rule: remove missing values only when nonmissing values exist, retaining multiple distinct values as ambiguity. The unused legacy mode() has no consumer and is omitted.
Point conversion retains all original coordinate columns. Numeric coercion has the legacy missing-coordinate behavior (na.fail = FALSE); malformed text raises a coercion warning; the original text remains in the raw source targets. No coordinate swap, range clipping, or inferred sign correction is introduced.
The fields ending in Contains use st_intersects(), including boundary intersections. The sparse result is checked at matching row indices, giving the same diagonal as the legacy dense matrix without allocating that matrix. An empty point produces NA, while a nonempty point against an empty polygon produces zero. The input CRS and global s2 setting remain unchanged.
s6_clinic_location_unique_nonNA_fn <- function(x) {
  x <- unique(x)
  if (any(is.na(x)) && !all(is.na(x))) x <- stats::na.omit(x)
  x
}
s6_clinic_location_read_fn <- function(archive, member) {
  s3_dictionary_archive_read_fn(archive, member, function(path) {
    read.csv(path, colClasses = "character", fileEncoding = "UTF-8",
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  })
}
s6_clinic_location_points_fn <- function(x) {
  x <- as.data.frame(x)
  for (source in c("sect", "mdss", "who", "unicef", "gps")) {
    columns <- paste0(source, c("_x", "_y"))

}
s6_clinic_location_intersects_fn <- function(points, polygons) {
  stopifnot(length(points) == length(polygons))
  hits <- sf::st_intersects(points, polygons)
  result <- as.numeric(vapply(seq_along(hits), function(i) i %in% hits[[i]], logical(1)))
  result[sf::st_is_empty(points)] <- NA_real_
  result
}

Tip Procedure: Identify A Unique Matching FKT



Keep the combined minimum-name-distance, <= 0.12 or name-containment, and minimum-geographic-distance condition. A single FKT qualifies independently of that condition. Distances retain the legacy comma and kilometer-string conversion. sum() and name min() retain missing values; ties or missing evidence may prevent a unique match rather than force a winner. Name containment uses stringi’s ICU regex matcher, the same regex engine used by stringr, with missing patterns propagated as NA. A missing clinic name becomes the pattern in the reverse containment test; stringr rejects that pattern before matching. Retaining NA preserves unknown evidence and the separate single-FKT rule without dropping assignment rows or filling missing names with empty strings.
s6_clinic_location_fkt_candidates_fn <- function(sect) {
  sect %>% filter(fkt_name != "" & !is.na(fkt_name)) %>%
    mutate(name_noPre = gsub("CSB1 |CSB2 |HP_|HP |FSP_|FSP_ |FSP ", "", fs_name),
      fkt_fs_stringdist = stringdist::stringdist(tolower(name_noPre), tolower(fkt_name), method = "cosine"),
      name_contain = stringi::stri_detect_regex(tolower(name_noPre), tolower(fkt_name)) |
        stringi::stri_detect_regex(tolower(fkt_name), tolower(name_noPre)),
      dist = gsub(",", ".", distance_csb_fkt) %>%
        gsub("Km|Km| km|km", "", .) %>% na_if("") %>% as.numeric()) %>%
    group_by(fs_uid) %>%
    mutate(n_fkt = n(),
      match_name_dist = (fkt_fs_stringdist == min(fkt_fs_stringdist) &
        (fkt_fs_stringdist <= 0.12 | name_contain) & dist == min(dist, na.rm = TRUE)) | n_fkt == 1,
      n_match = sum(match_name_dist)) %>% ungroup()
}

    fraction = sum(values, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(!is.na(values)))
}))

title: 24  Combine Reporting and Spatial Clinic Metadata
text:
This page implements 7_combine_clinic_metadata.R at revision 31e0769683e133e136b09ac0c6608c5a12657a9a. It produces monthly reporting metadata and clinic-level spatial attributes. All transformations are targets; rendering does not execute them. The final tables are nonspatial Parquet products, while page 23 retains the healthshed geometry handoff.






Important Prerequisite: Require The Reporting, Identity, And Spatial Handoffs






Dependency
Producing page
Contract

22

s2_clinic_ids_df

The reviewed neighbor-pairing CSV is an exact member of the already tracked s2_clinic_months_raw_zip. Source reads reuse the private extraction helper. Run scientific target builds only on the compute node. The checks below use synthetic fixtures or read completed targets; they never build the pipeline.








Tip Procedure: Record Coordinate Policy And Declare Helpers



Reviewed policy: preserve legacy missing coordinates for UNICEF. Both unicef and unicef2 retain missing coordinates in S7 even when S6 selected a valid UNICEF candidate. The policy is a tracked target, and the coordinate status explicitly identifies these rows. Other labels ending in 2 use their stored source pair; the original label remains in gps_source_raw.
Centroids use the same sf::st_centroid() operation and input CRS as the legacy script. Only the selected, nonempty geometries need calculation. No new projection, geodesic algorithm, or point-on-surface rule is introduced. Empty geometries yield missing coordinates. The spatial runtime from page 23 remains a dependency of location extraction and centroid calculation.
s7_clinic_coordinate_policy_list <- list(
  unicef = "legacy_missing",
  centroid = "legacy_st_centroid_input_crs",
  legacy_revision = "31e0769683e133e136b09ac0c6608c5a12657a9a")
s7_clinic_centroid_xy_fn <- function(geometry) {
  result <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = length(geometry), ncol = 2L,
                   dimnames = list(NULL, c("x", "y")))
  present <- which(!sf::st_is_empty(geometry))
  if (length(present)) {
    result[present, ] <- sf::st_coordinates(sf::st_centroid(geometry[present]))[, c("X", "Y"), drop = FALSE]
  }
  result
}
s7_clinic_selected_coordinates_fn <- function(locations, policy) {
  stopifnot(identical(policy$unicef, "legacy_missing"))
  label <- sub("2$", "", as.character(locations$which_use))
  result <- tibble::tibble(fs_uid = locations$fs_uid,
    gps_source_raw = as.character(locations$which_use), which_use = label,
    clinic_x = rep(NA_real_, nrow(locations)), clinic_y = rep(NA_real_, nrow(locations)))
  for (source in c("who", "mdss", "sect", "gps")) {
    selected <- which(label == source)
    if (length(selected)) {
      result$clinic_x[selected] <- as.numeric(locations[[paste0(source, "_x")]][selected])
      result$clinic_y[selected] <- as.numeric(locations[[paste0(source, "_y")]][selected])
    }
  }
  selected <- which(label == "fkt_centroid")
  if (length(selected)) {
    xy <- s7_clinic_centroid_xy_fn(locations$fkt_geometry[selected])
    result$clinic_x[selected] <- xy[, "x"]
    result$clinic_y[selected] <- xy[, "y"]
  }
  result
}
s7_clinic_reporting_long_fn <- function(tracker) {
  tracker %>% tidyr::pivot_longer(!clinic_ID, names_to = "year_month", values_to = "fname") %>%
    tidyr::separate_wider_position(year_month, widths = c(1, year = 4, 2, month = 2), cols_remove = FALSE) %>%
    mutate(across(c(year, month), as.numeric))
}








Tip Procedure: Reshape The Reporting Calendar And Attach Database Codes



Read the compact reporting tracker, retaining every existing calendar column and its fname == 0 rows. Do not manufacture months absent from the tracker. The historical join uses clinic, year, month, and source file together. Code strings retain their leading zeros. A missing code is filled with the clinic UID only for reported months in 2020 or later, as in the legacy script.
The join retains repeated historical rows. The reporting-key audit exposes expansion instead of silently choosing a code or deleting duplicate rows. database_code_origin records the UID fallback separately from a historical crosswalk code. year_month remains in the long intermediate for checks.
s7_clinic_reporting_track_df <- duckplyr::read_parquet_duckdb(
  s4a_clinic_reporting_track_parquet, prudence = "stingy") %>% collect()
s7_clinic_reporting_long_df <- s7_clinic_reporting_long_fn(s7_clinic_reporting_track_df)
s7_clinic_reporting_metadata_df <- s7_clinic_reporting_long_df %>%
  select(-year_month) %>%
  left_join(s2_clinic_ids_df %>% transmute(clinic_ID, year = cAnnee, month = cPeriode,
    fname, clinic_database_code = as.character(cCodeStru)),
    by = c("clinic_ID", "year", "month", "fname")) %>%
  mutate(database_code_origin = case_when(
      !is.na(clinic_database_code) ~ "historical_crosswalk",
      is.na(clinic_database_code) & fname != 0 & year >= 2020 ~ "reported_uid_fallback",
      TRUE ~ "missing"),
    clinic_database_code = ifelse(is.na(clinic_database_code) & fname != 0 & year >= 2020,
      clinic_ID, clinic_database_code))








Tip Procedure: Summarize Reporting And Apply Attribute Precedence



The clinic-level population includes only clinics with at least one retained report. n_month counts distinct reported calendar labels; first_report and last_report use those zero-padded labels, not a duration calculation.
Sectorization attributes win when present. The historical fallback uses all records tied at cAnnee + cPeriode / 13’s maximum, then the legacy distinct attribute projection. The shared unique_nonNA() helper retains multiple nonmissing values. Neither source ambiguity nor tied latest descriptions is reduced to first(); audits expose those conditions before interpreting the result as one record per clinic.
Ownership is a legacy heuristic: a nonmissing sectorization type other than FSP implies public, with ID_checked as fallback. It is computed before historical type fallback, preserving the original order. Normalize FSP_ as in the source. The added origin fields describe this precedence; they do not claim a validated ownership or facility-type history.
s7_clinic_reporting_summary_df <- s7_clinic_reporting_long_df %>%
  filter(fname != 0) %>%
  summarise(n_month = n_distinct(year_month), first_report = min(year_month),
            last_report = max(year_month), .by = clinic_ID)
s7_clinic_sectorization_attributes_df <- s5_sectorization_2022_clean_sf %>%
  sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
  summarise(across(c(region_uid:district_name, fs_type, fs_name, f_or_nf),
                   s6_clinic_location_unique_nonNA_fn), .by = fs_uid)
s7_clinic_latest_historical_attributes_df <- s2_clinic_ids_df %>%
  filter((cAnnee + cPeriode / 13) == max(cAnnee + cPeriode / 13), .by = clinic_ID) %>%
  select(clinic_ID, fs_name2 = cNom, fs_type2 = type_map, ID_checked) %>% distinct()
s7_clinic_metadata_attributes_df <- s7_clinic_reporting_summary_df %>%
  left_join(s7_clinic_sectorization_attributes_df, by = c("clinic_ID" = "fs_uid")) %>%
  left_join(s7_clinic_latest_historical_attributes_df, by = "clinic_ID") %>%
  mutate(across(c(fs_type, fs_type2), ~gsub("FSP_", "FSP", .x)),
    fs_name_origin = case_when(!is.na(fs_name) ~ "sectorization_2022",
      !is.na(fs_name2) ~ "latest_historical", TRUE ~ "missing"),
    fs_type_origin = case_when(!is.na(fs_type) ~ "sectorization_2022",
      !is.na(fs_type2) ~ "latest_historical", TRUE ~ "missing"),
    pub_priv_origin = case_when(!is.na(fs_type) ~ "sectorization_type_heuristic",
      !is.na(ID_checked) ~ "id_checked_heuristic", TRUE ~ "missing"),
    pub_priv = ifelse(fs_type != "FSP", "public", "private"),
    pub_priv2 = ifelse(ID_checked, "public", "private"),
    fs_type = ifelse(is.na(fs_type), fs_type2, fs_type),
    fs_name = ifelse(is.na(fs_name), fs_name2, fs_name),
    pub_priv = ifelse(is.na(pub_priv), pub_priv2, pub_priv)) %>%
  select(-fs_type2, -fs_name2, -pub_priv2)








Tip Procedure: Extract Coordinates And Fill The Selected Healthshed Centroids



Attach healthshed geometry and the selected-coordinate table by clinic UID. These ordinary dataframe intermediates retain an sfc column while geometry is needed. A selected healthshed centroid is computed after that join. The raw selection label remains distinct from the normalized display label.
coordinate_status distinguishes an available pair, the deliberate UNICEF parity gap, an absent location decision, and other missing selected pairs. It does not label a missing coordinate successful because S6 chose a source.
s7_clinic_selected_coordinates_df <- {
  s5_spatial_runtime_list
  s7_clinic_selected_coordinates_fn(s6_clinic_locations_selected_sf, s7_clinic_coordinate_policy_list)
}
s7_clinic_metadata_located_df <- s7_clinic_metadata_attributes_df %>%
  left_join(as.data.frame(select(s5_healthshed_clinic_final_sf, clinic_ID = fs_uid, geometry)),
            by = "clinic_ID") %>%
  left_join(s7_clinic_selected_coordinates_df, by = c("clinic_ID" = "fs_uid"))
s7_clinic_metadata_centroid_filled_df <- {
  s5_spatial_runtime_list
  x <- s7_clinic_metadata_located_df
  selected <- which(x$which_use == "shed_centroid")
  if (length(selected)) {
    xy <- s7_clinic_centroid_xy_fn(x$geometry[selected])
    x$clinic_x[selected] <- xy[, "x"]
    x$clinic_y[selected] <- xy[, "y"]
  }
  x %>% rename(healthshed_geometry = geometry) %>%
    mutate(coordinate_status = case_when(
      which_use == "unicef" ~ "legacy_unicef_missing",
      is.na(which_use) | which_use == "none" ~ "no_selected_location",
      !is.na(clinic_x) & !is.na(clinic_y) ~ "available_pair",
      TRUE ~ "missing_selected_pair"))
}








Tip Procedure: Retain Ownership Inference And Reviewed Neighbor Evidence



The final ownership fallback marks an otherwise unclassified clinic private when it reported since y2022_m01 and is absent from sectorization. The origin field names this inference. Historical comments about 36 such clinics are comparison observations, not assertions.
Read only the two reviewed pairing fields needed by the legacy join. Preserve missing and blank strings, duplicate pairing rows, and the join’s multiplicity; these are visible in the endpoint and final-key audits. A proposed neighbor does not replace the reporting clinic UID and no merge is performed.
s7_clinic_metadata_classified_df <- s7_clinic_metadata_centroid_filled_df %>%
  mutate(pub_priv_origin = ifelse(is.na(pub_priv) & last_report >= "y2022_m01" &
      !clinic_ID %in% s5_sectorization_2022_clean_sf$fs_uid,
      "recent_report_absent_sectorization_heuristic", pub_priv_origin),
    pub_priv = ifelse(is.na(pub_priv) & last_report >= "y2022_m01" &
      !clinic_ID %in% s5_sectorization_2022_clean_sf$fs_uid, "private", pub_priv))
s7_clinic_neighbor_member_chr <- s3_dictionary_archive_member_fn(s2_clinic_months_raw_zip,
  "data/raw/symphonia_verified/VERIFIED public_active_fs_missing_fkt.csv")

  s2_clinic_months_raw_zip, s7_clinic_neighbor_member_chr, function(path) {

  left_join(s7_clinic_neighbor_pairings_df, by = "clinic_ID") %>%
  mutate(has_healthshed = !sf::st_is_empty(healthshed_geometry)) %>%
  rename(gps_source = which_use) %>% select(-healthshed_geometry)








Tip Procedure: Expose Multiplicity, Calendar, And Pairing Audits



The monthly key and clinic-level key are claims to examine with these audits, not enforced by deleting repeated rows. The sectorization audit counts distinct nonmissing source values before summary; incompatible vector lengths may still raise the legacy summary error. The historical audit reports distinct tied latest descriptions. No audit rows are published during notebook rendering.
s7_clinic_reporting_key_audit_df <- s7_clinic_reporting_metadata_df %>%
  summarise(rows = n(), codes = n_distinct(clinic_database_code),
    sources = n_distinct(fname), .by = c(clinic_ID, year, month)) %>%
  filter(rows != 1 | is.na(clinic_ID) | is.na(year) | is.na(month) | month < 1 | month > 12)

  distinct(year_month, year, month) %>%
  mutate(valid_calendar = grepl("^y[0-9]{4}_m(0[1-9]|1[0-2])$", year_month))
s7_clinic_sectorization_attribute_audit_df <- s5_sectorization_2022_clean_sf %>%
  sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
  summarise(across(c(region_uid:district_name, fs_type, fs_name, f_or_nf),
    ~n_distinct(.x, na.rm = TRUE), .names = "{.col}_n_values"), .by = fs_uid) %>%
  filter(if_any(ends_with("_n_values"), ~.x > 1L))
s7_clinic_historical_attribute_audit_df <- s7_clinic_latest_historical_attributes_df %>%
  count(clinic_ID, name = "latest_descriptions") %>% filter(latest_descriptions > 1L)
s7_clinic_spatial_key_audit_df <- s7_clinic_spatial_metadata_df %>%
  count(clinic_ID, name = "rows") %>% filter(rows != 1 | is.na(clinic_ID))
s7_clinic_neighbor_audit_df <- s7_clinic_neighbor_pairings_df %>%
  add_count(clinic_ID, name = "pairing_rows") %>%
  mutate(source_in_metadata = clinic_ID %in% s7_clinic_reporting_summary_df$clinic_ID,
    neighbor_blank = !is.na(neighbor_to_merge) & trimws(neighbor_to_merge) == "",
    neighbor_missing = is.na(neighbor_to_merge),
    neighbor_in_metadata = neighbor_to_merge %in% s7_clinic_reporting_summary_df$clinic_ID,
    self_pair = !is.na(neighbor_to_merge) & clinic_ID == neighbor_to_merge)

The synthetic checks exercise reference transformations, code fallback, attribute precedence, selected coordinates and centroid handling, UNICEF parity, ownership, pairings, and Parquet round trips. Graph checks construct declarations without building targets.

After S7 runs on the compute node, use the following read-only EDA prompts in an authorized R session. These plain R examples are not tangled into the graph and do not run during rendering. They write no data and build no targets. The most recent archived data baseline selects the October 2024 ZIP data/clean/ CSVs for this stage; no newer final metadata exports were found. These predate the ZIP’s May 4, 2025 diagnosis family and must not be described as outputs associated with that run. Read identifiers as character and decode the old CSVs as CP1252; their accented text is not UTF-8. Fix comparison contracts before interpreting changed values as scientific disagreements.
Current scope (2026-11-08). The researcher reports that the initial shape checks on pages 18–21 appear to pass and considers shape checks sufficient to continue building. Begin with the side-by-side summaries below. Different source vintages can produce different dimensions and calendars; record those differences rather than forcing matching counts. The later value/provenance EDA is available when needed.
Are clinic sets, reporting calendars, and keys comparable? Inspect both sides’ multiplicity before joining. The new reporting tracker comes from S4; the archived script used an October 2024 intermediate tracker that differs from the selected ZIP’s May 4, 2025 diagnosis tracker. A calendar difference may therefore begin upstream.
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
archived_baseline <- dget(here::here("src", "archived-comparison-baseline.R"))
archive <- here::here(archived_baseline$archive_zip)
read_fn <- targets::tar_read(s3_dictionary_archive_read_fn)

})

  c(clinic_ID = "character", clinic_database_code = "character"))

Dimensions and key multiplicity for both metadata products. Added provenance columns can explain schema differences. For reporting metadata, the key is clinic/year/month; for spatial metadata, it is clinic.
# Shape check: metadata-dimensions
metadata_shape <- function(x, keys) tibble::tibble(
  rows = nrow(x), columns = length(names(x)),
  clinics = dplyr::n_distinct(x$clinic_ID, na.rm = TRUE),
  missing_key_rows = sum(!stats::complete.cases(x[keys])),
  unique_keys = nrow(dplyr::distinct(x, dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(keys)))),
  extra_key_rows = nrow(x) - nrow(dplyr::distinct(x, dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(keys))))
)
metadata_shapes <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  `most recent archived data` = dplyr::bind_rows(
    reporting = metadata_shape(old_time, c("clinic_ID", "year", "month")),
    spatial = metadata_shape(old_spatial, "clinic_ID"), .id = "product"),
  `current pipeline` = dplyr::bind_rows(
    reporting = metadata_shape(new_time, c("clinic_ID", "year", "month")),
    spatial = metadata_shape(new_spatial, "clinic_ID"), .id = "product"),
  .id = "source"
) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(source, product), names_to = "metric", values_to = "count") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = source, values_from = count) |>
  dplyr::mutate(difference = `current pipeline` - `most recent archived data`)
print(metadata_shapes, n = Inf)
# Shape check: metadata-schema
metadata_columns <- function(x) tibble::tibble(position = seq_along(names(x)), column = names(x))
dplyr::bind_rows(
  `most recent archived data` = dplyr::bind_rows(
    reporting = metadata_columns(old_time), spatial = metadata_columns(old_spatial), .id = "product"),
  `current pipeline` = dplyr::bind_rows(

) |>

Reporting rows per period and reporting status. An absent group contributes zero rows; difference is current minus archived. Repeated clinic-month keys inflate row counts, so inspect the multiplicity summary alongside this table. fname = 0 means nonreporting; a missing fname remains a separate category.

  `current pipeline` = new_time |> dplyr::count(year, month, reported = fname != 0, name = "rows"),
  .id = "source"
) |>

  dplyr::mutate(difference = `current pipeline` - `most recent archived data`) |>

Continue to clinic-set, repeated-key, and calendar evidence when needed:

Did reporting counts, codes, or source choices change for uniquely keyed records? Keep repeated keys outside the first paired comparison. Use explicit missing-value equality instead of dropping missing discrepancies with !=.

a <- old_time %>% filter(n() == 1, .by = all_of(time_keys))
b <- new_time %>% filter(n() == 1, .by = all_of(time_keys))

anti_join(b, a, by = time_keys)

paired_time %>% filter(!same(fname_old, fname_new) |
  !same(clinic_database_code_old, clinic_database_code_new))
# Check code provenance, including reported UID fallbacks and missing older codes:
new_time %>% count(year, reported = fname != 0, database_code_origin)
Are attribute and location differences traceable to a source? Restrict spatial-attribute pairing to one row per UID on both sides. Compare discrete fields first, then coordinate differences with an explicitly chosen tolerance. Inspect the raw source label, the normalized display label, and coordinate status together; unicef deliberately remains missing under the parity policy.
paired_spatial <- inner_join(old_spatial %>% filter(n() == 1, .by = clinic_ID),
  new_spatial %>% filter(n() == 1, .by = clinic_ID), by = "clinic_ID", suffix = c("_old", "_new"))

  compared = nrow(paired_spatial), changed = sum(!same(paired_spatial[[paste0(field, "_old")]],
    paired_spatial[[paste0(field, "_new")]])))))
paired_spatial %>% transmute(clinic_ID, gps_source_old, gps_source_new,
  x_missing_changed = is.na(clinic_x_old) != is.na(clinic_x_new),
  y_missing_changed = is.na(clinic_y_old) != is.na(clinic_y_new),
  delta_longitude = clinic_x_new - clinic_x_old, delta_latitude = clinic_y_new - clinic_y_old) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(delta_longitude)), desc(abs(delta_latitude))) %>% head(20)

title: 26  Clean and Harmonize the 2025–2026 Waves
text:
This page ports crosswalk_new_to_old.py, final_crosswalk.py, and build_w3_2025_26.py. Both deliveries and maximum reduction were authorized by the researcher. Python is reference evidence, never a runtime dependency.






Important Prerequisite: Require Pinned Inputs And The Existing Dictionary



Require page 26’s Stagecoach inventory, raw Parquet branches, and schemas. Reference names and X positions come from page 21’s ZIP-derived schema. M1–M5 follow Kai; ambiguous matches, overlapping source-name conflicts, and fuzzy suggestions are not applied. Review tables preserve exact source/file/name/period decisions with reviewer and reason. They are ordinary tracked R objects declared below. If reviewed files are supplied later, Stagecoach should stage them and this notebook should read them through file targets.








Tip Procedure: Port Name Matching And Period Conflicts



M1 is exact, M2 the three script-0 renames, M3 unique normalized text, M4 a common table wrapper, and M5 a same-table code remainder. Wrappers require at least half of a table’s names and at most four words, following Kai’s corrected rule. Demographic-only remainders cannot match. Fuzzy similarity supplies review suggestions only. File context is retained.
s9_new_wave_normalize_fn <- function(x) {
  x <- stringi::stri_replace_all_regex(stringi::stri_trans_nfkd(x), "\\p{M}", "")
  x <- trimws(gsub("\\s+", " ", tolower(gsub("[–—−]", "-", x)), perl = TRUE))
  gsub("\\s*,\\s*", ", ", gsub("\\s*-\\s*", "-", x, perl = TRUE), perl = TRUE)
}
s9_new_wave_aliases_fn <- function() setNames(
  c("T13: AME 0-6 mois", "T13: AME 1ère heure", "MIDs pour groupe à risque (migrants/réfugiés/personnes déplacées)"),
  c("T13: AME premiere heure 0-6 mois", "T13: AME premiere heure 1ère heure",
    "CHU CHRR T26 MIDs pour groupe à risque (migrants/réfugiés/personnes déplacées)"))
s9_new_wave_wrappers_fn <- function(x) {
  x <- unique(x)
  if(!length(x)) return(character())
  prefixes <- unlist(lapply(strsplit(s9_new_wave_normalize_fn(x), " ", fixed = TRUE), function(words) {
    if (length(words) < 2L) return(character())
    vapply(seq_len(min(4L, length(words)-1L)), function(n) paste(head(words,n), collapse=" "), "")
  }), use.names=FALSE)
  if(!length(prefixes)) return(character())
  counts <- table(prefixes)
  hits <- names(counts)[counts >= length(x)*0.5]
  hits[order(-nchar(hits), hits)]
}
s9_new_wave_remainders_fn <- function(name, wrappers) {
  if(!length(wrappers)) return(character())
  name <- s9_new_wave_normalize_fn(name)
  hits <- wrappers[startsWith(name, paste0(wrappers," "))]
  if(!length(hits)) return(character())
  rem <- substring(name,nchar(hits)+2L)
  demo <- "^([0-9<>=+.,()/-]*|[0-9].*|masculin|feminin|homme|femme|ans?|mois|j|jours|m|et|plus)$"
  rem[vapply(strsplit(rem," ",fixed=TRUE),function(words) any(!grepl(demo,words)),TRUE)]
}
s9_new_wave_old_headers_fn <- function(paths) {
  paths <- paths[grepl("/RMA 2024/",paths,fixed=TRUE)]
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(paths,function(path) tibble::tibble(
    table_key=s8_new_wave_table_key_fn(path),
    source_name=setdiff(s8_new_wave_header_fn(path),s8_new_wave_metadata_fn())))) |> dplyr::distinct()
}
s9_new_wave_candidates_fn <- function(headers, reference, old_headers) {
  reference <- setdiff(reference,c(s8_new_wave_metadata_fn(),"V1","code_fs","TYPE","FS"))
  items <- headers |> dplyr::filter(!is_metadata) |> dplyr::distinct(table_key,source_name)
  aliases <- s9_new_wave_aliases_fn(); normalized <- s9_new_wave_normalize_fn(reference)
  canonical <- function(x) ifelse(x %in% names(aliases),unname(aliases[x]),x)
  code <- "^t([0-9]+)(\\s+[ivx]+(-[0-9]+)?)?\\s*:\\s*-?\\s*"
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(items)),function(i) {
    name <- items$source_name[[i]]; key <- items$table_key[[i]]; norm <- s9_new_wave_normalize_fn(name)
    hits <- character(); method <- "unmatched"
    if (name %in% reference) { hits <- name; method <- "M1 exact" }
    if (!length(hits)) {
      hits <- intersect(unname(aliases[s9_new_wave_normalize_fn(names(aliases)) == norm]),reference)
      if (length(hits)) method <- "M2 script0"
    }
    if (!length(hits)) { hits <- reference[normalized == norm]; if (length(hits)) method <- "M3 normalised" }
    if (!length(hits)) {
      olds <- unique(old_headers$source_name[old_headers$table_key == key])
      news <- unique(items$source_name[items$table_key == key])
      rem <- s9_new_wave_remainders_fn(name,s9_new_wave_wrappers_fn(news))
      if (length(rem)) hits <- unique(canonical(olds[vapply(olds,function(old)
        any(c(s9_new_wave_normalize_fn(old),s9_new_wave_remainders_fn(old,s9_new_wave_wrappers_fn(olds))) %in% rem),TRUE)]))
      hits <- intersect(hits,reference); if (length(hits)) method <- "M4 wrapper"
    }
    if (!length(hits)) {
      table <- regmatches(key,regexec("tableau ([0-9]+)",key))[[1L]]
      if (length(table) == 2L) {
        codes <- regmatches(normalized,regexec(code,normalized))
        same_table <- vapply(codes,function(x) length(x)>1L && x[[2L]] == table[[2L]],TRUE)
        rem <- c(s9_new_wave_remainders_fn(name,s9_new_wave_wrappers_fn(items$source_name[items$table_key == key])),
                 if (grepl(code,norm)) sub(code,"",norm))
        hits <- reference[same_table & sub(code,"",normalized) %in% rem]
        if (length(hits)) method <- "M5 table code"
      }
    }
    hits <- unique(hits); if (length(hits)>1L) method <- "ambiguous"
    suggestions <- if (!length(hits) && length(reference)) {
      score <- stringdist::stringsim(norm,normalized,method="jw")
      paste(head(reference[order(-score,reference)],3L),collapse=" || ")
    } else paste(hits,collapse=" || ")
    tibble::tibble(table_key=key,source_name=name,target_name=if(length(hits)==1L) hits else NA_character_,
      method=method,n_options=length(hits),candidates=suggestions)
  }))
}
s9_new_wave_mapping_fn <- function(headers,candidates,review,reference,config) {
  stopifnot(all(c("source_id","relative_path","source_name","target_name","valid_from","valid_to","decision","reviewer","reason") %in% names(review)))
  x <- headers |> dplyr::filter(!is_metadata) |> tidyr::unnest_longer(periods,values_to="periodcode") |>
    dplyr::mutate(periodcode=suppressWarnings(as.integer(periodcode))) |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(periodcode),periodcode>=config$start_period,periodcode<=config$end_period) |>
    dplyr::left_join(candidates,by=c("table_key","source_name"),relationship="many-to-one")
  x$reviewer <- NA_character_; x$review_reason <- NA_character_
  if (nrow(review)) {
    stopifnot(all(review$decision %in% c("accept","reject")),
      all(!is.na(review$reviewer) & nzchar(review$reviewer)),all(!is.na(review$reason) & nzchar(review$reason)),
      all(!is.na(review$valid_from) & !is.na(review$valid_to)),
      all(grepl("^[0-9]{4}(0[1-9]|1[0-2])$",c(review$valid_from,review$valid_to))),
      all(as.integer(review$valid_from)<=as.integer(review$valid_to)))
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(x))) {
      relative <- substring(x$source_file[[i]],nchar(x$source_id[[i]])+2L)
      hits <- which(review$source_name==x$source_name[[i]] & review$source_id %in% c("*",x$source_id[[i]]) &
        review$relative_path %in% c("*",relative) & as.integer(review$valid_from)<=x$periodcode[[i]] &
        as.integer(review$valid_to)>=x$periodcode[[i]])
      if (!length(hits)) next
      specificity <- (review$source_id[hits]!="*")+(review$relative_path[hits]!="*")
      hits <- hits[specificity==max(specificity)]
      if (length(hits)!=1L) stop("Overlapping mapping review decisions.")
      j <- hits[[1L]]
      if (review$decision[[j]]=="accept" && !review$target_name[[j]] %in% reference) stop("Reviewed target outside recorded schema.")
      x$target_name[[i]] <- if(review$decision[[j]]=="accept") review$target_name[[j]] else NA_character_
      x$method[[i]] <- paste("R reviewed",review$decision[[j]])
      x$reviewer[[i]] <- review$reviewer[[j]]; x$review_reason[[i]] <- review$reason[[j]]
    }
  }
  x |> dplyr::group_by(periodcode,target_name) |>
    dplyr::mutate(conflict=!is.na(target_name) & dplyr::n_distinct(source_name)>1L) |>
    dplyr::ungroup() |> dplyr::mutate(applied=!is.na(target_name) & !conflict)
}








Tip Procedure: Parse Tokens And Reduce Measurements In DuckDB



Each CSV is unpivoted with null cells retained. Numeric coercion follows Kai, with invalid/nonfinite tokens counted per source column. Missing/invalid UID or YYYYMM keys fail. Valid out-of-scope periods are counted as exclusions. Duplicate measurements take maxima; all-missing maxima remain missing. Metadata uses first nonmissing values in source/file/record order, with conflicting metadata fields counted rather than hidden.
s9_new_wave_unpivot_sql_fn <- function(path) {
  source <- s4a_diagnosis_read_fn(path)
  columns <- s4a_diagnosis_columns_fn(paste("SELECT * FROM",source))
  stopifnot(all(c("organisationunitid","periodcode","periodname") %in% columns))
  measured <- setdiff(columns,c(s8_new_wave_metadata_fn(),"_source_id","_source_file","_source_row","_source_md5"))
  if (!length(measured)) stop("Source CSV has no measurement columns.")
  paste0("SELECT * FROM (SELECT * FROM ",source,") UNPIVOT INCLUDE NULLS (raw_value FOR source_name IN (",
    paste(s8_new_wave_identifier_fn(measured),collapse=","),"))")
}
s9_new_wave_parse_fn <- function(raw,mapping,config,path) {
  source <- s4a_diagnosis_read_fn(raw)
  keys <- s4a_diagnosis_query_fn(paste0("SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE organisationunitid IS NULL OR ",
    "trim(organisationunitid) IN ('','NA') OR periodcode IS NULL OR NOT regexp_full_match(periodcode, ",
    "'[0-9]{4}(0[1-9]|1[0-2])')) AS invalid_keys, count(*) FILTER (WHERE try_cast(periodcode AS INTEGER) ",
    "NOT BETWEEN ",config$start_period," AND ",config$end_period,") AS outside_period_rows FROM ",source)) |> dplyr::collect()
  if (keys$invalid_keys>0) stop("Source has missing/invalid UID or YYYYMM keys; inspect raw input.")
  file <- s4a_diagnosis_query_fn(paste("SELECT DISTINCT _source_file FROM",source)) |> dplyr::collect()
  stopifnot(nrow(file)==1L)
  m <- mapping[mapping$source_file==file$`_source_file`,c("source_name","periodcode","target_name","method","applied")]
  map_path <- tempfile(fileext=".parquet"); on.exit(unlink(map_path),add=TRUE)
  duckplyr::compute_parquet(duckplyr::as_duckdb_tibble(unique(as.data.frame(m))),map_path)
  token <- "trim(raw_value)"
  missing <- paste0(token," IS NULL OR ",token," IN (",paste(s8_new_wave_literal_fn(config$missing_tokens),collapse=","),")")
  parsed <- paste0("WITH cells AS (",s9_new_wave_unpivot_sql_fn(raw),") SELECT *, CASE WHEN ",missing,
    " THEN NULL WHEN isfinite(try_cast(",token," AS DOUBLE)) THEN try_cast(",token,
    " AS DOUBLE) ELSE NULL END AS value, NOT (",missing,") AND (try_cast(",token,
    " AS DOUBLE) IS NULL OR NOT isfinite(try_cast(",token," AS DOUBLE))) AS invalid_numeric FROM cells")
  audit <- sub("[.]parquet$","_numeric_audit.parquet",path); key_audit <- sub("[.]parquet$","_key_audit.parquet",path)
  s4a_diagnosis_write_fn(paste0("SELECT _source_file,source_name,count(*) AS rows,count(*) FILTER (WHERE value IS NULL) AS missing_values,",
    "count(*) FILTER (WHERE invalid_numeric) AS invalid_numeric,count(*) FILTER (WHERE value=0) AS zeros,",
    "count(*) FILTER (WHERE value<0) AS negatives FROM (",parsed,") GROUP BY ALL"),audit)
  duckplyr::compute_parquet(duckplyr::as_duckdb_tibble(dplyr::bind_cols(file,keys)),key_audit)
  s4a_diagnosis_write_fn(paste0("SELECT c.organisationunitid,try_cast(c.periodcode AS INTEGER) AS periodcode,",
    "m.target_name,c.source_name,c.value,c.invalid_numeric,c._source_file,c._source_row FROM (",parsed,") c JOIN ",
    s4a_diagnosis_read_fn(map_path)," m ON c.source_name=m.source_name AND try_cast(c.periodcode AS INTEGER)=m.periodcode WHERE m.applied"),path)
  c(typed=path,numeric_audit=audit,key_audit=key_audit)
}
s9_new_wave_reduce_fn <- function(paths,path) s4a_diagnosis_write_fn(paste0(
  "SELECT organisationunitid,periodcode,target_name,max(value) AS value,count(*) AS input_cells,",
  "count(DISTINCT _source_file) AS source_files,count(DISTINCT value) AS distinct_values,",
  "count(*) FILTER (WHERE invalid_numeric) AS invalid_numeric FROM ",s4a_diagnosis_read_fn(paths),
  " GROUP BY organisationunitid,periodcode,target_name"),path)
s9_new_wave_reports_fn <- function(raw,reduced,schema,config,path) {
  source <- s4a_diagnosis_read_fn(raw)
  columns <- s4a_diagnosis_columns_fn(paste("SELECT * FROM",source))
  present <- intersect(setdiff(s8_new_wave_metadata_fn(),c("organisationunitid","periodcode")),columns)
  normalized <- function(col) paste0("CASE WHEN trim(",s8_new_wave_identifier_fn(col),") IN (",
    paste(s8_new_wave_literal_fn(config$missing_tokens),collapse=","),") THEN NULL ELSE ",s8_new_wave_identifier_fn(col)," END")
  projection <- vapply(present,function(col) paste0("first(",normalized(col),
    " ORDER BY _source_file,_source_row) FILTER (WHERE ",normalized(col)," IS NOT NULL) AS ",s8_new_wave_identifier_fn(col)),"")
  conflicts <- vapply(present,function(col) paste0("(count(DISTINCT ",normalized(col),")>1)::INTEGER"),"")
  codes <- if("organisationunitcode" %in% columns) paste0("count(DISTINCT ",normalized("organisationunitcode"),
    ") AS source_code_count,list(DISTINCT ",normalized("organisationunitcode")," ORDER BY ",normalized("organisationunitcode"),
    ") FILTER (WHERE ",normalized("organisationunitcode")," IS NOT NULL) AS source_code_candidates") else
    "0::INTEGER AS source_code_count,NULL::VARCHAR[] AS source_code_candidates"
  excluded <- schema$w3_description[schema$w3_colname %in% c("X1708","X1709")]
  eligibility <- paste0("SELECT organisationunitid,periodcode,bool_or(coalesce(value>0,false) AND target_name NOT IN (",
    paste(s8_new_wave_literal_fn(c(excluded,"__not_a_measurement__")),collapse=","),")) AS eligible FROM ",
    s4a_diagnosis_read_fn(reduced)," GROUP BY organisationunitid,periodcode")
  s4a_diagnosis_write_fn(paste0("WITH meta AS (SELECT organisationunitid,try_cast(periodcode AS INTEGER) AS periodcode,",
    paste(projection,collapse=","),",",paste(conflicts,collapse="+")," AS metadata_conflicts,",codes,",count(DISTINCT _source_file) AS source_files FROM ",
    source," WHERE try_cast(periodcode AS INTEGER) BETWEEN ",config$start_period," AND ",config$end_period,
    " GROUP BY organisationunitid,periodcode), eligible AS (",eligibility,") SELECT m.*,coalesce(e.eligible,false) AS reported ",
    "FROM meta m LEFT JOIN eligible e USING (organisationunitid,periodcode)"),path)
}








Tip Procedure: Declare Audited Handoffs



s9_new_wave_mapping_review_df <- tibble::tibble(
  source_id = character(), relative_path = character(), source_name = character(),
  target_name = character(), valid_from = character(), valid_to = character(),
  decision = character(), reviewer = character(), reason = character()
)
s9_new_wave_old_headers_df <- s9_new_wave_old_headers_fn(s0_clinic_RMA_W3_raw_paths_chr)
s9_new_wave_mapping_candidates_df <- s9_new_wave_candidates_fn(s8_new_wave_schema_df,
  s3_w3_column_dictionary_df$w3_description,s9_new_wave_old_headers_df)
s9_new_wave_mapping_audit_df <- s9_new_wave_mapping_fn(s8_new_wave_schema_df,s9_new_wave_mapping_candidates_df,

s9_new_wave_typed_paths_chr <- s9_new_wave_typed_parquet[!grepl("_audit[.]parquet$",s9_new_wave_typed_parquet)]
s9_new_wave_numeric_audit_paths_chr <- s9_new_wave_typed_parquet[grepl("_numeric_audit[.]parquet$",s9_new_wave_typed_parquet)]
s9_new_wave_key_audit_paths_chr <- s9_new_wave_typed_parquet[grepl("_key_audit[.]parquet$",s9_new_wave_typed_parquet)]
#| format: file
s9_new_wave_mapping_audit_parquet <- s5_healthshed_write_table_fn(s9_new_wave_mapping_audit_df,
  here::here("data/intermediates/new_wave/mapping_audit.parquet"))
s9_new_wave_numeric_audit_parquet <- s4a_diagnosis_write_fn(paste("SELECT * FROM",
  s4a_diagnosis_read_fn(s9_new_wave_numeric_audit_paths_chr)),here::here("data/intermediates/new_wave/numeric_audit.parquet"))

s9_new_wave_measurement_availability_parquet <- s4a_diagnosis_write_fn(paste0(
  "SELECT periodcode,target_name,count(*) AS clinic_months,count(value) AS measured,count(*) FILTER (WHERE value IS NULL) AS missing_values,",
  "sum(invalid_numeric) AS invalid_numeric,count(*) FILTER (WHERE value=0) AS zeros FROM ",
  s4a_diagnosis_read_fn(s9_new_wave_clinic_month_parquet)," GROUP BY periodcode,target_name"),

title: 27  Locate Clinics and Assemble the Final Database
text:
This page ports Kai’s unseen-clinic inventory, clinical projection, and reviewed NA correction boundaries. Stable source UIDs are retained; name and district matches are candidates only. Existing healthsheds remain explicitly labelled 2022 references. Missing coordinates do not remove clinical records.






Important Prerequisite: Require Audited Measurements And Reviewed Overrides



Require pages 25–27. Identity reviews and NA corrections are ordinary tracked R tables declared here. Identity reviews have source_uid,clinic_ID,valid_from,valid_to,decision,reviewer,reason; decisions are accept or exclude, with inclusive YYYYMM bounds. No row is guessed from a normalized name. NA corrections have file,var,period_from,period_to,reason,reviewer, matching Kai’s correction input with explicit reviewer provenance. Empty inputs apply no corrections.
The final reporting interface uses one row per clinic-month. Where historical codes conflict, preserve all candidates in an audit and expose a missing scalar code plus an ambiguity flag. This is a representation of uncertainty, not selection of a winning code or a change to historical diagnosis values.








Tip Procedure: Resolve Stable UIDs And Expose Predecessor Candidates



s10_new_wave_identity_fn <- function(reports,review,existing,path) {
  stopifnot(all(c("source_uid","clinic_ID","valid_from","valid_to","decision","reviewer","reason") %in% names(review)))
  x <- duckplyr::read_parquet_duckdb(reports,prudence="stingy") |>
    dplyr::distinct(organisationunitid,periodcode) |> dplyr::collect() |>
    dplyr::rename(source_uid=organisationunitid) |>
    dplyr::mutate(clinic_ID=source_uid,identity_status=ifelse(source_uid %in% existing,"existing_uid","new_uid"),decision="retain")
  x$reviewer <- NA_character_; x$review_reason <- NA_character_
  if (nrow(review)) {
    stopifnot(all(review$decision %in% c("accept","exclude")),
      all(!is.na(review$reviewer) & nzchar(review$reviewer)),all(!is.na(review$reason) & nzchar(review$reason)),
      all(!is.na(review$valid_from) & !is.na(review$valid_to)),
      all(grepl("^[0-9]{4}(0[1-9]|1[0-2])$",c(review$valid_from,review$valid_to))),
      all(as.integer(review$valid_from)<=as.integer(review$valid_to)))
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(x))) {
      hits <- which(review$source_uid==x$source_uid[[i]] & as.integer(review$valid_from)<=x$periodcode[[i]] & as.integer(review$valid_to)>=x$periodcode[[i]])
      if (!length(hits)) next
      if (length(hits)!=1L) stop("Overlapping identity decisions.")
      j <- hits[[1L]]
      if (review$decision[[j]]=="accept" && (is.na(review$clinic_ID[[j]]) || !nzchar(trimws(review$clinic_ID[[j]])))) stop("Reviewed clinic ID is empty.")
      x$clinic_ID[[i]] <- if(review$decision[[j]]=="accept") review$clinic_ID[[j]] else NA_character_
      x$identity_status[[i]] <- paste0("reviewed_",review$decision[[j]])
      x$decision[[i]] <- review$decision[[j]]
      x$reviewer[[i]] <- review$reviewer[[j]]; x$review_reason[[i]] <- review$reason[[j]]
    }
  }
  s5_healthshed_write_table_fn(x,path)
}
s10_new_wave_predecessors_fn <- function(reports,old_w3,existing) {
  cols <- c("organisationunitid","organisationunitname","orgunitlevel3")
  new <- duckplyr::read_parquet_duckdb(reports,prudence="stingy") |>
    dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(cols)) |> dplyr::distinct() |> dplyr::collect()
  old <- duckplyr::read_parquet_duckdb(old_w3,prudence="stingy") |>
    dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(cols)) |> dplyr::distinct() |> dplyr::collect()
  key <- function(x) gsub("[^a-z0-9]+"," ",s9_new_wave_normalize_fn(x)) |> trimws()
  new <- new |> dplyr::filter(!organisationunitid %in% existing) |>
    dplyr::mutate(name_key=key(organisationunitname),district_key=key(orgunitlevel3))
  old <- old |> dplyr::mutate(name_key=key(organisationunitname),district_key=key(orgunitlevel3))
  dplyr::inner_join(dplyr::filter(new,!is.na(name_key),nzchar(name_key),!is.na(district_key),nzchar(district_key)),
    old,by=c("name_key","district_key"),suffix=c("_new","_old"),relationship="many-to-many") |>
    dplyr::mutate(applied=FALSE,evidence="same normalized name and district; candidate only")
}

Tip Procedure: Project Clinical Definitions And Apply Guarded Corrections



Use the existing dictionary’s wave3B expressions and V/filename assignments. Known negative repairs and refrigerator reporting exclusions use the recorded schema descriptions, not a newly sorted header. For sums, an all-missing set of components remains missing; measured zero remains zero. This prevents the false zeros Kai later repairs when source measurements are unavailable. Other negative and sentinel values retain their source semantics.
Corrections create new outputs from immutable upstream products. They fail before writing if a rule names an unknown variable or would overwrite a nonzero value. There is no in-place editing or _before backup dependency.
s10_new_wave_expression_fn <- function(terms) {
  if (!length(terms)) return("CAST(NULL AS DOUBLE)")
  q <- s8_new_wave_identifier_fn(terms)
  if (length(q)==1L) return(q)
  paste0("CASE WHEN ",paste(paste0(q," IS NOT NULL"),collapse=" OR ")," THEN ",
    paste(paste0("coalesce(",q,",0)"),collapse="+")," ELSE NULL END")
}
s10_new_wave_diagnosis_fn <- function(group,measurements,reports,identity,rules,schema,corrections,config,path) {
  stopifnot(all(c("file","var","period_from","period_to","reason","reviewer") %in% names(corrections)))
  allowed <- rules[rules$wave=="wave3B",c("filename","var")]
  stopifnot(all(paste(corrections$file,corrections$var,sep="/") %in% paste(allowed$filename,allowed$var,sep="/")))
  r <- rules[rules$wave=="wave3B" & rules$filename==group,]
  stopifnot(nrow(r)>0L,!anyDuplicated(r$var))
  terms <- unique(unlist(r$terms,use.names=FALSE))
  stopifnot(all(terms %in% schema$w3_colname))
  descriptions <- schema$w3_description[match(terms,schema$w3_colname)]
  fixed <- schema$w3_description[schema$w3_colname %in% c("X1067","X1068","X1736")]
  eligible <- paste0("SELECT DISTINCT i.clinic_ID,r.periodcode FROM ",s4a_diagnosis_read_fn(reports),
    " r JOIN ",s4a_diagnosis_read_fn(identity)," i ON r.organisationunitid=i.source_uid AND r.periodcode=i.periodcode ",
    "WHERE r.reported AND i.decision<>'exclude'")
  canonical <- paste0("SELECT i.clinic_ID,m.periodcode,m.target_name,max(CASE WHEN m.target_name IN (",
    paste(s8_new_wave_literal_fn(c(fixed,"__not_a_measurement__")),collapse=","),") AND m.value<0 THEN NULL ELSE m.value END) AS value FROM ",
    s4a_diagnosis_read_fn(measurements)," m JOIN ",s4a_diagnosis_read_fn(identity),
    " i ON m.organisationunitid=i.source_uid AND m.periodcode=i.periodcode WHERE i.decision<>'exclude' GROUP BY ALL")
  pivot <- if(length(terms)) paste0("PIVOT canonical ON target_name IN (",
    paste(paste0(s8_new_wave_literal_fn(descriptions)," AS ",s8_new_wave_identifier_fn(terms)),collapse=","),
    ") USING max(value) GROUP BY clinic_ID,periodcode") else "SELECT DISTINCT clinic_ID,periodcode FROM canonical"
  values <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(r)),function(i) paste0(s10_new_wave_expression_fn(r$terms[[i]]),
    "::DOUBLE AS ",s8_new_wave_identifier_fn(r$var[[i]])),"")
  sql <- paste0("WITH canonical AS (",canonical,"),eligible AS (",eligible,"),wide AS (",pivot,
    ") SELECT e.clinic_ID,(e.periodcode//100)::INTEGER AS cAnnee,(e.periodcode%100)::INTEGER AS cPeriode,",
    config$fname,"::INTEGER AS fname,",paste(values,collapse=",")," FROM eligible e LEFT JOIN wide w USING(clinic_ID,periodcode)")
  corrections <- corrections[corrections$file==group,]
  if(nrow(corrections)) {
    stopifnot(all(corrections$var %in% r$var),all(!is.na(corrections$reviewer) & nzchar(corrections$reviewer)),
      all(!is.na(corrections$reason) & nzchar(corrections$reason)),
      all(!is.na(corrections$period_from) & !is.na(corrections$period_to)),
      all(grepl("^[0-9]{4}(0[1-9]|1[0-2])$",c(corrections$period_from,corrections$period_to))),
      all(as.integer(corrections$period_from)<=as.integer(corrections$period_to)))
    for(i in seq_len(nrow(corrections))) {
      c <- corrections[i,]; column <- s8_new_wave_identifier_fn(c$var)
      period <- paste0("(cAnnee*100+cPeriode) BETWEEN ",as.integer(c$period_from)," AND ",as.integer(c$period_to))
      bad <- s4a_diagnosis_query_fn(paste0("SELECT count(*) n FROM (",sql,") WHERE ",period," AND ",column," IS NOT NULL AND ",column,"<>0")) |> dplyr::collect()
      if(bad$n>0) stop("NA correction would replace a nonzero measurement.")
      sql <- paste0("SELECT * REPLACE(CASE WHEN ",period," THEN NULL ELSE ",column," END AS ",column,") FROM (",sql,")")
    }
  }
  s4a_diagnosis_write_fn(sql,path)
}
s10_final_diagnosis_fn <- function(group,old_paths,new_paths,path) {
  old <- old_paths[basename(old_paths)==paste0(group,".parquet")]
  new <- new_paths[basename(new_paths)==paste0(group,".parquet")]
  stopifnot(length(old)==1L,length(new)==1L,
    identical(s4a_diagnosis_columns_fn(paste("SELECT * FROM",s4a_diagnosis_read_fn(old))),
              s4a_diagnosis_columns_fn(paste("SELECT * FROM",s4a_diagnosis_read_fn(new)))))
  overlap <- s4a_diagnosis_query_fn(paste0("SELECT count(*) n FROM ",s4a_diagnosis_read_fn(old),
    " a JOIN ",s4a_diagnosis_read_fn(new)," b USING(clinic_ID,cAnnee,cPeriode)")) |> dplyr::collect()
  if(overlap$n>0) stop("Historical and new diagnosis periods overlap; review source selection before appending.")
  s4a_diagnosis_write_fn(paste0("SELECT * FROM ",s4a_diagnosis_read_fn(old)," UNION ALL SELECT * FROM ",s4a_diagnosis_read_fn(new)),path)
}








Tip Procedure: Build Reporting Calendars And Retain Code Ambiguity



Reporting eligibility follows the historical positive-measurement rule; source presence and source-period coverage are separate flags. The calendar ends at the latest observed source period, with missing intervening months labelled explicitly. New clinics are not assigned a historical ownership or facility-type history. Excluded UIDs remain in the identity audit.
s10_new_wave_reporting_fn <- function(reports,identity,config) {
  x <- duckplyr::read_parquet_duckdb(reports,prudence="stingy") |> dplyr::collect()
  ids <- duckplyr::read_parquet_duckdb(identity,prudence="stingy") |> dplyr::collect()
  x <- dplyr::inner_join(x,ids,by=c("organisationunitid"="source_uid","periodcode"),relationship="one-to-one") |>
    dplyr::filter(decision!="exclude")
  get <- function(name) if(name %in% names(x)) as.character(x[[name]]) else rep(NA_character_,nrow(x))
  x$clinic_database_code <- ifelse(x$reported,ifelse(is.na(get("organisationunitcode")) | !nzchar(get("organisationunitcode")),x$organisationunitid,get("organisationunitcode")),NA_character_)
  x$database_code_origin <- ifelse(x$reported,"new_delivery_code_or_uid",NA_character_)
  ambiguous <- x$source_code_count>1L & x$reported
  x$clinic_database_code[ambiguous] <- NA_character_
  x$database_code_origin[ambiguous] <- "ambiguous_new_source_codes_in_reports"
  x$fname <- ifelse(x$reported,as.integer(config$fname),0L)
  x$year <- x$periodcode%/%100L; x$month <- x$periodcode%%100L
  x$source_report_present <- TRUE; x$source_covered <- TRUE
  x$database_code_ambiguous <- ambiguous
  x
}
s10_reporting_resolve_fn <- function(x) {
  keys <- c("clinic_ID","year","month")
  stopifnot(!anyNA(x[keys]))
  if(!"database_code_ambiguous" %in% names(x)) x$database_code_ambiguous <- FALSE
  repeated <- duplicated(x[keys]) | duplicated(x[keys],fromLast=TRUE)
  out <- x[!duplicated(x[keys]),,drop=FALSE]
  audit <- x[repeated,,drop=FALSE]
  if(any(repeated)) {
    groups <- audit |> dplyr::group_by(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(keys))) |> dplyr::group_split()
    for(g in groups) {
      sources <- unique(g$fname[g$fname!=0L])
      if(length(sources)>1L) stop("A clinic-month has conflicting report sources.")
      at <- which(out$clinic_ID==g$clinic_ID[[1L]] & out$year==g$year[[1L]] & out$month==g$month[[1L]])
      codes <- unique(stats::na.omit(g$clinic_database_code))
      ambiguous <- length(codes)>1L || any(g$database_code_ambiguous,na.rm=TRUE)
      out$fname[at] <- if(length(sources)) sources else 0L
      for(flag in intersect(c("source_report_present","source_covered"),names(out))) out[[flag]][at] <- any(g[[flag]],na.rm=TRUE)
      out$clinic_database_code[at] <- if(length(codes)==1L && !ambiguous) codes else NA_character_
      out$database_code_ambiguous[at] <- ambiguous
      origins <- unique(stats::na.omit(g$database_code_origin))
      out$database_code_origin[at] <- if(length(origins)==1L) origins else if(length(origins)>1L) "multiple_origins_in_audit" else NA_character_
      if(ambiguous) out$database_code_origin[at] <- "ambiguous_candidates_in_audit"
    }
  }
  list(data=out,audit=audit)
}
s10_final_reporting_fn <- function(old,new) {
  old$source_report_present <- old$fname!=0L; old$source_covered <- TRUE
  old$database_code_ambiguous <- FALSE
  fields <- c("clinic_ID","year","month","fname","clinic_database_code","database_code_origin",
    "database_code_ambiguous","source_report_present","source_covered")
  for(field in setdiff(fields,names(old))) old[[field]] <- NA_character_
  old <- old[fields]; new <- new[fields]
  overlap <- dplyr::inner_join(dplyr::distinct(old,year,month),dplyr::distinct(new,year,month),by=c("year","month"))
  if(nrow(overlap)) stop("Historical and new reporting calendars overlap.")
  resolved <- s10_reporting_resolve_fn(dplyr::bind_rows(old,new))
  x <- resolved$data
  covered <- unique(x$year*100L+x$month)
  population <- unique(x$clinic_ID[x$fname!=0L])
  dates <- as.Date(sprintf("%04d-%02d-01",x$year,x$month))
  calendar <- seq(min(dates),max(dates),by="month")
  grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(clinic_ID=population,date=calendar) |>
    dplyr::mutate(year=as.integer(format(date,"%Y")),month=as.integer(format(date,"%m"))) |> dplyr::select(-date)
  result <- dplyr::left_join(grid,x,by=c("clinic_ID","year","month"),relationship="one-to-one") |>
    dplyr::mutate(source_report_present=dplyr::coalesce(source_report_present,FALSE),
      source_covered=(year*100L+month) %in% covered,fname=dplyr::coalesce(as.integer(fname),0L),
      database_code_ambiguous=dplyr::coalesce(database_code_ambiguous,FALSE))
  list(data=result,audit=resolved$audit)
}
s10_final_spatial_fn <- function(reporting,old,new_reports,healthsheds,config) {
  summaries <- reporting |> dplyr::filter(fname!=0L) |>
    dplyr::mutate(year_month=sprintf("y%04d_m%02d",year,month)) |>
    dplyr::summarise(n_month=dplyr::n(),first_report=min(year_month),last_report=max(year_month),.by=clinic_ID)
  attrs <- old |> dplyr::select(-dplyr::any_of(c("n_month","first_report","last_report")))
  missing <- setdiff(summaries$clinic_ID,attrs$clinic_ID)
  new <- new_reports[match(missing,new_reports$clinic_ID),,drop=FALSE]
  field <- function(name) if(name %in% names(new)) as.character(new[[name]]) else rep(NA_character_,length(missing))
  extra <- tibble::tibble(clinic_ID=missing,fs_name=field("organisationunitname"),region_name=field("orgunitlevel2"),
    district_name=field("orgunitlevel3"),commune_name=field("orgunitlevel4"),fs_name_origin="new_delivery",
    clinic_x=NA_real_,clinic_y=NA_real_,gps_source=NA_character_,coordinate_status="no_new_location_evidence")
  attrs <- dplyr::bind_rows(attrs,extra)
  good <- healthsheds$fs_uid[!sf::st_is_empty(healthsheds)]
  dplyr::left_join(summaries,attrs,by="clinic_ID",relationship="one-to-one") |>
    dplyr::mutate(has_healthshed=clinic_ID %in% good,
      healthshed_reference_year=ifelse(has_healthshed,as.integer(config$historical_healthshed_year),NA_integer_),
      healthshed_temporal_status=ifelse(has_healthshed,"historical_reference","no_healthshed_evidence"))
}

Tip Procedure: Validate The Final Database Before Packaging



Compare complete key multisets in DuckDB and collect scalar counts only. Every diagnosis group must match its dictionary schema, have unique, nonmissing clinic-month keys, and agree with the common reporting key set. Reporting and spatial keys must be unique. Geometry coverage is represented by explicit flags; empty historical polygons remain review evidence rather than a reason to drop nonspatial observations.
schecks_key_difference_fn <- function(a,b) {
  s4a_diagnosis_query_fn(paste0("SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM ((",a,") EXCEPT ALL (",b,
    "))) AS left_only,(SELECT count(*) FROM ((",b,") EXCEPT ALL (",a,"))) AS right_only")) |> dplyr::collect()
}
schecks_final_shape_fn <- function(paths,dictionary,reporting,spatial,healthsheds) {
  paths <- paths[!grepl("_wrong_fname[.]parquet$",paths)]
  groups <- unique(stats::na.omit(dictionary$filename))
  stopifnot(length(paths)==length(groups),setequal(tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(paths)),groups))
  key <- "clinic_ID,cAnnee,cPeriode,fname"
  reference <- paste0("SELECT ",key," FROM ",s4a_diagnosis_read_fn(paths[[1L]]))
  report_keys <- reporting |> dplyr::filter(fname!=0L) |>
    dplyr::transmute(clinic_ID,cAnnee=as.integer(year),cPeriode=as.integer(month),fname=as.integer(fname))
  scratch <- tempfile(fileext=".parquet"); on.exit(unlink(scratch),add=TRUE)
  s5_healthshed_write_table_fn(report_keys,scratch)
  report_diff <- schecks_key_difference_fn(reference,paste0("SELECT ",key," FROM ",s4a_diagnosis_read_fn(scratch)))
  rows <- lapply(paths,function(path) {
    group <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(path)); source <- s4a_diagnosis_read_fn(path)
    columns <- s4a_diagnosis_columns_fn(paste("SELECT * FROM",source))
    expected <- c("clinic_ID","cAnnee","cPeriode","fname",dictionary$var[!is.na(dictionary$filename) & dictionary$filename==group])
    differences <- schecks_key_difference_fn(paste0("SELECT ",key," FROM ",source),reference)
    counts <- s4a_diagnosis_query_fn(paste0("SELECT count(*) AS rows, count(*) FILTER (WHERE clinic_ID IS NULL OR trim(clinic_ID)='' OR ",
      "cAnnee IS NULL OR cPeriode IS NULL OR fname IS NULL OR cPeriode NOT BETWEEN 1 AND 12) AS missing_keys, ",
      "(SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT clinic_ID,cAnnee,cPeriode FROM ",source," GROUP BY ALL HAVING count(*)>1)) AS repeated_keys FROM ",source)) |> dplyr::collect()
    tibble::tibble(resource=group,rows=counts$rows,schema_matches=identical(columns,expected),
      missing_keys=counts$missing_keys,repeated_keys=counts$repeated_keys,
      key_differences=differences$left_only+differences$right_only,
      ok=identical(columns,expected) && counts$missing_keys==0 && counts$repeated_keys==0 && all(differences==0))
  })
  time_keys <- reporting[c("clinic_ID","year","month")]
  spatial_keys <- spatial["clinic_ID"]
  good <- healthsheds$fs_uid[!sf::st_is_empty(healthsheds)]
  geometry_agrees <- identical(as.logical(spatial$has_healthshed),spatial$clinic_ID %in% good)
  additional <- tibble::tibble(resource=c("reporting","spatial","reported_key_agreement","geometry_flags"),
    rows=c(nrow(reporting),nrow(spatial),nrow(report_keys),nrow(healthsheds)),schema_matches=TRUE,
    missing_keys=c(sum(!stats::complete.cases(time_keys)),sum(!stats::complete.cases(spatial_keys)),0L,0L),
    repeated_keys=c(sum(duplicated(time_keys)),sum(duplicated(spatial_keys)),0L,0L),
    key_differences=c(0L,0L,sum(unlist(report_diff)),sum(spatial$has_healthshed != (spatial$clinic_ID %in% good))),
    ok=c(!anyNA(time_keys) && !anyDuplicated(time_keys),!anyNA(spatial_keys) && !anyDuplicated(spatial_keys) &&
      setequal(spatial$clinic_ID,report_keys$clinic_ID),all(report_diff==0),geometry_agrees))
  valid <- sf::st_is_valid(healthsheds)
  geometry <- tibble::tibble(resource="geometry_structure",rows=nrow(healthsheds),schema_matches=!is.na(sf::st_crs(healthsheds)),
    missing_keys=sum(is.na(healthsheds$fs_uid) | healthsheds$fs_uid==""),repeated_keys=sum(duplicated(healthsheds$fs_uid)),
    key_differences=sum(!valid | is.na(valid)),
    ok=!is.na(sf::st_crs(healthsheds)) && all(!is.na(valid) & valid) && !anyNA(healthsheds$fs_uid) &&
      all(nzchar(healthsheds$fs_uid)) && !anyDuplicated(healthsheds$fs_uid))
  dplyr::bind_rows(dplyr::bind_rows(rows),additional,geometry)
}

Tip Procedure: Port Kai's Source And Renaming Seam Diagnostics



Two comparisons mirror break_check.py: December 2024/January 2025 with December 2023/January 2024 as baseline; and May/June 2025 with May/June 2024 as baseline. National sums retain all-missing as missing. The exploratory 30-positive-clinic and ratio-of-ratios thresholds are labels, not release acceptance criteria or authority to change a mapping.
schecks_seam_fn <- function(group,paths,dictionary,path,min_positive=30L,lower=0.8,upper=1.25) {
  input <- paths[basename(paths)==paste0(group,".parquet")]; stopifnot(length(input)==1L)
  vars <- dictionary$var[!is.na(dictionary$filename) & dictionary$filename==group]
  seams <- list(A_source_change=c(202412L,202501L,202312L,202401L),B_renaming=c(202505L,202506L,202405L,202406L))
  queries <- lapply(names(seams),function(name) {
    periods <- seams[[name]]
    long <- paste0("SELECT * FROM (SELECT cAnnee*100+cPeriode AS periodcode,",paste(s8_new_wave_identifier_fn(vars),collapse=","),
      " FROM ",s4a_diagnosis_read_fn(input)," WHERE cAnnee*100+cPeriode IN (",paste(periods,collapse=","),
      ")) UNPIVOT INCLUDE NULLS (value FOR var IN (",paste(s8_new_wave_identifier_fn(vars),collapse=","),"))")
    totals <- paste0("SELECT var,periodcode,sum(value) AS total,count(*) FILTER (WHERE value>0) AS positive FROM (",long,") GROUP BY ALL")
    columns <- unlist(lapply(seq_along(periods),function(i) c(
      paste0("max(total) FILTER (WHERE periodcode=",periods[[i]],") AS total",i),
      paste0("max(positive) FILTER (WHERE periodcode=",periods[[i]],") AS positive",i))))
    universe <- paste0("SELECT * FROM (VALUES ",paste(paste0("(",s8_new_wave_literal_fn(vars),")"),collapse=","),") v(var)")
    paste0("WITH totals AS (",totals,"), universe AS (",universe,"), stats AS (SELECT var,",paste(columns,collapse=","),
      " FROM universe LEFT JOIN totals USING(var) GROUP BY var), ratios AS (SELECT *,total2/nullif(total1,0) AS ratio,total4/nullif(total3,0) AS ratio_baseline FROM stats), ",
      "result AS (SELECT *,ratio/nullif(ratio_baseline,0) AS ratio_of_ratios,coalesce(positive1>=",min_positive,
      " AND positive2>=",min_positive,",false) AS testable FROM ratios) SELECT ",s8_new_wave_literal_fn(group),
      " AS file,",s8_new_wave_literal_fn(name)," AS seam,*,testable AND (ratio_of_ratios IS NULL OR ratio_of_ratios NOT BETWEEN ",
      lower," AND ",upper,") AS listed FROM result")
  })
  s4a_diagnosis_write_fn(paste(paste0("(",queries,")"),collapse=" UNION ALL "),path)
}
The execution page branches this diagnostic by diagnosis group. The older investigations below are retained as future comparison contracts; they are not production gates and do not introduce Feather readers.








Tip Procedure: Classify The Deferred Legacy Investigations Before Porting Them










Legacy responsibility
Planned owner and evidence




Export/file/schema inventories
Page 17 and schecks_source_export_tables_list; record periods, columns, and source provenance


Reader experiments
Page 18’s reader tests plus schecks_csv_reader_comparison_list; explain encoding, sparse typing, quotes, and name repair


Wave 3 preparation comparisons
This page; keyed equality and discrepancy summaries against a fixed prepared reference


Dictionary comparisons
This page; expressions, ordered schemas, translations, and harmonized IDs evaluated separately


Mumps year/subset exports
Explicit optional diagnostic projections in procedures, stored as targets/Parquet outside the raw tree


Transformation-specific assertions
The check block of the page that owns the transformation



The repeated late-2023 comparison that reads a 2022 object needs a corrected, explicit source selection before it can support a conclusion. The exploratory numeric matrix that compares the old object with itself cannot establish old/new agreement. Do not carry those mistakes into a regression test.








Tip Procedure: Build Small Alignment And Schema Contracts



Use schecks_w3_legacy_comparison_inputs_list and schecks_dictionary_legacy_comparison_inputs_list as small reference/path contracts rather than lists of fully loaded measurement tables. Record ordered names, types, row grain, key uniqueness, and source hashes or tracked target identities in schecks_migration_contract_list.
Validate keys before sorting or joining: a many-to-many join can multiply rows and disguise a mismatch. When legitimate repeated keys exist, define their comparison unit explicitly rather than assigning a new row number whose order differs between storage engines. Check equality of key sets and multiplicity before comparing values.
Use page 21’s recorded X schema to compare dictionary references. Ignore a legacy export index only when it is proven to be an IO artifact, not a scientific identifier. Never renumber V or X variables merely to make the tables look equal.








Tip Procedure: Compare Large Measurement Products In DuckDB



Read tracked Parquet paths as relations. Project a limited variable set or period partition, align on the agreed keys, and compute counts of missing keys and unequal values. Collect only small summaries for the manager. Persist governed discrepancy records as schecks_w3_value_mismatches_parquet when row-level evidence is needed.
The plan replaces full in-memory comparison matrices with keyed comparison relations. Test the comparator itself using unequal fixtures: new-only and old-only rows, duplicate keys, permuted row order, changed numeric values, and differing missing values must produce failures or explicit discrepancy records. A passing self-comparison is only a sanity check.
Compare entered zero, missing, -1, and -99 separately according to the owning transformation’s contract. Do not convert all missing values to infinity or all logical columns to numeric as an unexplained equality fix.








Tip Procedure: Compare Dictionary Semantics Before Output Labels



Build schecks_dictionary_migration_report_df from the new dictionary, its recorded source schemas, and the chosen legacy reference. Compare the wave expressions, repeated summands, unavailable-wave semantics, output groups, French descriptions, and English translation provenance separately.
If V numbering differs, first compare the ordered inputs and expression identity. Produce an explicit old/new expression crosswalk for review rather than rewriting either dictionary. An apparent translation-only difference must not conceal a changed clinical definition or age band.
Reuse page 21’s synthetic validator and archive-translation coverage checks. Do not invoke a live translation service during validation to refresh the reference or fill a comparison gap.








Tip Procedure: Keep Mumps Diagnostic Projections Outside The Raw Tree



Inventory the combined 2021–2022 mumps export in schecks_mumps_source_df only if small enough for the stated memory budget; otherwise use a source file target and DuckDB relation. Separate year views in schecks_mumps_by_year_list and the named 2021 male 2–11-month projection in schecks_mumps_2021_males_2_11m_df, or persist their larger equivalents as schecks_mumps_output_parquet.
Preserve the exact source header T4: Oreillon 2-11m, Masculin, period filter, and metadata-column selection. Check year coverage and the relationship of the subset to its parent without writing oreillon_2021.csv or other derived files back into data/inputs.
These are diagnostic projections unless explicitly adopted as a curation input. If a repair becomes authoritative, implement it in the owning source preparation procedure and add a visible dependency to pages 18 or 22. It must not enter the analysis through an undocumented raw-directory side effect.








Tip Procedure: Assemble A Migration Evidence Report



schecks_migration_report_list will combine small reports from identities, dictionary construction, diagnoses, spatial assignments, locations, and the two metadata products. Larger row-level evidence remains in tracked Parquet; geometry comparisons remain in ordinary spatial targets.







Report field
Required content




Provenance
Input/reference revisions, code revision, environment and geometry-engine versions


Alignment
Grain, keys, key counts/multiplicity, and column/schema correspondence


Results
Exact matches, measured discrepancies, missing coverage, and resource observations


Decisions
Accepted differences, rationale, accountable review, and unresolved items


Artifacts
Target names and tracked evidence paths; no ambiguous scratch filenames



Keep validation separate from release approval. This evidence informs the release contract; it does not authorize publishing protected data or decide a scientific discrepancy on the reviewer’s behalf.








Warning Check: Specify Evidence And Comparator Acceptance



Before wiring the deferred archive-value comparators, create tests/check-migration-comparators.R. Current final-product and seam helpers are exercised by tests/check-new-wave-pipeline.R. The tests must show that each comparator detects an injected mismatch, handles missing values and legitimate multiplicity according to its contract, and does not report equality when its two inputs differ.
After a separately authorized build, the final checks should confirm:

every required comparison has identifiable inputs and a completed result;
key coverage, schema references, and expression/sentinel tests satisfy the approved contract;
each remaining discrepancy is either an accepted, documented change or an unresolved failure that prevents an equivalence claim;
parallel and serial execution produce the same canonically compared data;
a second build with unchanged inputs rebuilds no scientific targets;
evidence artifacts exist, remain under governed destinations, and can be inspected without loading all measurements into R.

Historical numerical comments in data_checks.R are comparison hypotheses, not newly observed outcomes. No comparison or scientific pipeline has been executed while writing this plan.
