title: 29  Inventory and Package a Versioned Release
text:
Packaging consumes pages 26–30’s final curated products. The default is an internal candidate in canonical Parquet, with explicit schemas and source, code, and environment provenance. It is not an external publication action. No CSV/Feather compatibility export or public disclosure policy is inferred.






Important Prerequisite: Require Passing Final Contracts



All final shape/key checks must pass. Unavailable measurements remain missing; ambiguous historical codes retain their candidates and ambiguity flags. Missing new-clinic locations remain explicit. Geometry is a 2022 reference. A version is immutable: changed data, code, or resource selection requires a new version, including after a partially completed package attempt.








Tip Procedure: Declare Tracked R Release Parameters



srelease_parameters_list <- list(
  name = "mdg-healthshed-clinic-data",
  title = "Madagascar Healthshed Clinic Data",
  version = "0.1.0",
  previous_version = NULL,
  change = "initial",
  notes = "Initial versioned Parquet data package.",
  access = "internal",
  status = "candidate",
  prohibited_columns = character()
)
The release name is stable across versions. The initial release is 0.1.0; access and status remain separate metadata. Following KiribatiBiomarkers, release directories use vMAJOR.MINOR.BUGFIX under data/outputs/releases/, starting with data/outputs/releases/v0.1.0/. Package metadata stores the unprefixed version (0.1.0). BUGFIX is the semantic-version PATCH component; numeric components have no leading zeroes or suffixes:








Change
Increment
Examples




Breaking for external collaborators
MAJOR; reset MINOR and PATCH
Renamed/removed columns, changed keys, units, geometry interpretation, or resource paths


Non-breaking addition
MINOR; reset PATCH
Additional periods, clinics, diagnoses, or optional fields compatible with existing readers


Bug fix
PATCH
Corrected values or metadata without changing the interface



For subsequent releases set previous_version, choose change as major, minor, or patch, and record the reason in notes. The validator checks the exact increment. The researcher classifies compatibility with collaborators; schema inspection alone cannot determine whether a scientific meaning changed. Existing data/processed/0.1.0-internal/ artifacts remain historical candidates.
The spatial resource carries WKT at 17-digit precision, CRS WKT, the facility UID, empty-geometry status and reference year. It is ordinary Parquet with an explicit spatial schema, not an implied GeoParquet or shapefile export. The ordinary sf target remains available for native R consumers.








Tip Procedure: Prepare Resource Schemas And Provenance



srelease_parameters_fn <- function(config) {
  valid <- function(x) is.character(x) && length(x)==1L && !is.na(x) &&
    grepl("^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)[.](0|[1-9][0-9]*)[.](0|[1-9][0-9]*)$",x)
  if(!valid(config$version)) stop("Release version must be MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH without leading zeroes.")
  if(length(config$name)!=1L || is.na(config$name) ||
     !grepl("^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$",config$name)) stop("Invalid release name.")
  if(length(config$title)!=1L || is.na(config$title) || !nzchar(config$title) ||
     length(config$notes)!=1L || is.na(config$notes) || !nzchar(config$notes)) stop("Release title and notes are required.")
  if(is.null(config$previous_version)) {
    if(!identical(config$change,"initial")) stop("Initial release must declare change = initial.")
  } else {
    if(!valid(config$previous_version) || !config$change %in% c("major","minor","patch")) stop("Declare the previous semantic version and change category.")
    parts <- as.numeric(strsplit(config$previous_version,".",fixed=TRUE)[[1L]])
    i <- match(config$change,c("major","minor","patch"))
    parts[[i]] <- parts[[i]]+1
    if(i<3L) parts[(i+1L):3L] <- 0
    if(!identical(config$version,paste(parts,collapse="."))) stop("Version does not match the declared semantic increment.")
  }
  invisible(config)
}
srelease_directory_fn <- function(root,config) {
  srelease_parameters_fn(config)
  file.path(root,paste0("v",config$version))
}
srelease_geometry_fn <- function(x,year,path) {
  table <- tibble::tibble(fs_uid=as.character(x$fs_uid),geometry_wkt=sf::st_as_text(sf::st_geometry(x),digits=17),
    crs_wkt=sf::st_crs(x)$wkt,is_empty=sf::st_is_empty(x),reference_year=as.integer(year))
  s5_healthshed_write_table_fn(table,path)
}
srelease_provenance_fn <- function(files,source_inventory,config,archive) {
  packages <- c("targets","duckdb","duckplyr","sf","dplyr","tidyr","frictionless","jsonlite")
  baseline <- dget(here::here("src/archived-comparison-baseline.R"))
  archive_sha256 <- srelease_sha256_fn(archive)
  if(!identical(archive_sha256,baseline$archive_sha256)) stop("Historical archive differs from the reviewed freeze.")
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    tibble::tibble(component=paste0("file:",files),value=unname(tools::md5sum(files))),
    tibble::tibble(component=paste0("package:",packages),value=vapply(packages,function(p) as.character(utils::packageVersion(p)),"")),
    tibble::tibble(component=c("R","source_inventory_sha256","historical_archive_sha256","release_version","access","status"),
      value=c(as.character(getRversion()),srelease_sha256_fn(source_inventory),archive_sha256,config$version,config$access,config$status)))
}
srelease_resources_fn <- function(diagnoses,dictionary,reporting,spatial,geometry,schema_audit,mapping_audit,
  identity,codes,availability,seams,provenance,source_inventory,numeric_audit,key_audit,predecessors,reviews,reports) {
  named <- c(setNames(diagnoses,paste0("by_diagnosis/",basename(diagnoses))),
    diagnosis_dictionary=dictionary,clinic_reporting_metadata=reporting,clinic_spatial_metadata=spatial,
    healthsheds2022=geometry,`audits/final_shape`=schema_audit,`audits/mapping`=mapping_audit,
    `audits/identity`=identity,`audits/reporting_code_candidates`=codes,`audits/availability`=availability,
    setNames(seams,paste0("audits/seams/",basename(seams))),provenance=provenance,source_inventory=source_inventory,
    `audits/numeric`=numeric_audit,`audits/source_keys`=key_audit,`audits/predecessor_candidates`=predecessors,
    `audits/review_inputs`=reviews,`audits/new_source_reports`=reports)
  names(named) <- ifelse(endsWith(names(named),".parquet"),names(named),paste0(names(named),".parquet"))
  stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(names(named)),all(file.exists(named)))
  lapply(seq_along(named),function(i) list(name=names(named)[[i]],source=unname(named[[i]])))
}
srelease_sha256_fn <- function(path) {
  out <- system2("sha256sum",shQuote(path),stdout=TRUE)
  stopifnot(length(out)==1L,is.null(attr(out,"status")),grepl("^[a-f0-9]{64}",out))
  substr(out,1L,64L)
}
srelease_contract_fn <- function(resources,shape,config,root) {
  srelease_parameters_fn(config)
  stopifnot(identical(config$access,"internal"),identical(config$status,"candidate"))
  if(!nrow(shape) || !all(shape$ok)) stop("Final product checks failed; inspect the governed shape audit.")
  stopifnot(length(resources)>0L)
  contract <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(resources,function(x) {
    if(grepl("^/|(^|/)\\.\\.(/|$)",x$name)) stop("Unsafe release resource name.")
    columns <- s4a_diagnosis_columns_fn(paste("SELECT * FROM",s4a_diagnosis_read_fn(x$source)))
    if(any(columns %in% config$prohibited_columns)) stop("Release resource contains a prohibited field.")
    tibble::tibble(resource=x$name,source_sha256=srelease_sha256_fn(x$source),
      release_name=config$name,version=config$version,title=config$title,
      previous_version=if(is.null(config$previous_version)) NA_character_ else config$previous_version,
      change=config$change,notes=config$notes,access=config$access,status=config$status)
  })) |> dplyr::arrange(resource)
  directory <- srelease_directory_fn(root,config); path <- file.path(directory,"_contract.parquet")
  if(file.exists(path)) {
    old <- duckplyr::read_parquet_duckdb(path,prudence="stingy") |> dplyr::collect() |> dplyr::arrange(resource)
    if(!isTRUE(all.equal(as.data.frame(old),as.data.frame(contract),check.attributes=FALSE))) stop("Immutable release version differs; select a new version.")
    return(path)
  }
  if(dir.exists(directory) && length(list.files(directory,all.files=TRUE,no..=TRUE))) stop("Nonempty release has no matching immutable contract.")
  s5_healthshed_write_table_fn(contract,path)
}
srelease_copy_fn <- function(resource,contract,config,root) {
  stopifnot(file.exists(contract))
  manifest <- duckplyr::read_parquet_duckdb(contract,prudence="stingy") |> dplyr::collect()
  row <- manifest[manifest$resource==resource$name,]
  stopifnot(nrow(row)==1L,identical(srelease_sha256_fn(resource$source),row$source_sha256))
  destination <- file.path(srelease_directory_fn(root,config),resource$name)
  if(file.exists(destination)) {
    if(!identical(srelease_sha256_fn(destination),row$source_sha256)) stop("Existing immutable resource differs.")
    return(destination)
  }
  dir.create(dirname(destination),recursive=TRUE,showWarnings=FALSE)
  temporary <- tempfile("package-",tmpdir=dirname(destination),fileext=".parquet")
  on.exit(unlink(temporary),add=TRUE)
  if(!file.copy(resource$source,temporary) || !identical(srelease_sha256_fn(temporary),row$source_sha256)) stop("Release copy failed checksum verification.")
  if(!file.rename(temporary,destination)) stop("Could not atomically install release resource.")
  destination
}
srelease_write_once_fn <- function(table,path) {
  if(file.exists(path)) {
    old <- duckplyr::read_parquet_duckdb(path,prudence="stingy") |> dplyr::collect()
    if(!isTRUE(all.equal(as.data.frame(old),as.data.frame(table),check.attributes=FALSE))) stop("Immutable release metadata differs.")
    return(path)
  }
  s5_healthshed_write_table_fn(table,path)
}

title: 30  Execute the Pipeline
text:
30.1 Parallel targets execution plan
The historical branch uses the hand-delivered May 2025 ZIP exclusively and dynamically branches the approved W3 CSV preparation and legacy clinic-month inventory work. Page 16 tracks that ZIP and extracts only its selected W3 and reviewed mapping sources; the Google Drive/rclone mirror is excluded from historical inputs and comparisons. Branching is declared here rather than in the transformation notebooks: each notebook defines one-file transformation logic, while this graph defines dependencies and the scheduler can distribute independent branches. Clinic-month branches track one Parquet file per monthly member of the staged ZIP. Page 20 combines their paths into a single Parquet inventory before collecting the reduced identity table. Page 21 constructs the cross-wave diagnosis dictionary from the prepared Wave 3 schema and archived source dictionaries and translations. Page 22 cleans and maps diagnosis measurements, selects report sources, and branches over dictionary output groups. S4 currently uses the existing serial runner; Slurm and controller configuration are outside this implementation. Page 23 reconciles the frozen sectorization and reviewed spatial corrections, constructs clinic healthsheds, and retains ordinary sf handoffs for pages 24–25. A cheap always-check target records the spatial package/native engine versions and s2 setting; changed values invalidate the spatial read. Page 24 assembles frozen coordinate sources, tests row-aligned intersections, and retains candidates and the selected source for page 25. Page 25 combines reporting history, reviewed spatial attributes, coordinate selection, and neighbor evidence into two tracked metadata Parquet products.
Pages 26–28 implement the separate 2025–2026 source survey, cleaning, and geospatial/final-aggregation work. Those deliveries are outside the old-wave ZIP. These pages are now included by tar_tangle() here. The graph includes both approved deliveries, final-product validation, internal candidate packaging, and independent resource verification. Declaring or rendering this graph does not execute it. Stagecoach owns the inputs; tracked R values in the notebooks own transformation and release parameters. No separate preparation step is needed.

title: 30  Execute the Pipeline
text:
Tip Procedure: Plan One Allocation With Local Target Workers



Planned configuration, not enabled by this page yet. Legacy stage 4B is absorbed into the existing runner and targets execution boundary. Submit one Slurm allocation through the page-15 launcher and run one tar_make() manager inside the project container. The manager will dispatch ready targets to local R worker processes within that allocation.
The planned backend is the supported crew local controller, selected through tar_option_set(controller = ...). The ordinary tar_make() call remains the execution entry point; it has no new worker-count argument. Do not port stage 4A’s future::plan(multicore), future_map() pools, or future.globals.maxSize overrides into individual targets. Do not submit one Slurm job for each diagnosis partition or use a Slurm worker-launcher plugin for this single-allocation plan.
Illustrative configuration for a future reviewed resource profile:
# Planning example only: not part of the emitted _targets.R below.
# Declare and lock crew through page 14 before enabling this configuration.
tar_option_set(
  controller = crew::crew_controller_local(workers = 2L)
)
Two workers are an example, not an established memory-safe default. Select the worker count from measured branch requirements and the approved allocation. The local controller creates separate R processes on the manager’s node; additional allocated nodes do not automatically become workers.








Tip Procedure: Plan Branch Memory, Threads, And Scheduling



Keep measurement-heavy operations inside bounded stage-4 targets and pass Parquet paths between them. Schedule independent monthly, complete-period, and output-group branches in parallel. Keep ordered spatial correction rounds and other dependent transformations in their scientific sequence.
Before activation, record a versioned resource profile with:







Resource
Required decision and verification




Allocation
One manager task, approved CPUs, total memory, wall time, and shared writable project/scratch storage


Worker concurrency
Explicit count within CPU and measured memory budgets, including manager overhead and retry behavior


Engine threads
Explicit per-worker DuckDB/BLAS thread budgets; do not give every worker the whole allocation’s CPU count


Memory
Branch peak R plus engine memory, manager memory, and headroom; engine settings alone are not evidence of total process memory


Files
Branch-unique outputs, private temporary extraction/scratch, and read-only shared inputs


Environment
Same container, project working directory, and locked R library in every worker; initialize connections inside each process



Use a representative month and output group as the first pilot. If a branch does not fit its budget, reduce its working set or partition it at a safe scientific boundary before increasing concurrency. Parallel execution does not divide the memory required by one oversized target. Do not request a blanket high-memory stage-4 job to compensate for collecting all waves in R.
Add crew to the direct dependency declaration and lock it only when the controller implementation is introduced. The current _targets.R, runner, and dependency lock remain unchanged by this detailed plan. The target graph shown below is the currently implemented graph; pages 18–30 and internal candidate packaging are now wired into it.

title: 31  Verify an Internal Candidate
text:
Verification reopens each candidate resource, compares its schema and complete row multiset with its curated source, and records checksums and row counts. It verifies serialization, not scientific equivalence with an archived release.






Important Prerequisite: Require The Immutable Resource Contract



Package copies must refer to the exact source hashes in the versioned contract. A changed source or modified package must fail verification. The default access remains internal and the release status remains candidate.








Tip Procedure: Verify Every Resource And Record Its Schema



srelease_verify_fn <- function(resource,package,contract,config) {
  manifest <- duckplyr::read_parquet_duckdb(contract,prudence="stingy") |> dplyr::collect()
  row <- manifest[manifest$resource==resource$name,]
  stopifnot(nrow(row)==1L,identical(srelease_sha256_fn(package),row$source_sha256),
    identical(srelease_sha256_fn(resource$source),row$source_sha256))
  a <- paste("SELECT * FROM",s4a_diagnosis_read_fn(resource$source))
  b <- paste("SELECT * FROM",s4a_diagnosis_read_fn(package))
  schema_a <- s4a_diagnosis_query_fn(paste("DESCRIBE",a)) |> dplyr::collect()
  schema_b <- s4a_diagnosis_query_fn(paste("DESCRIBE",b)) |> dplyr::collect()
  differences <- schecks_key_difference_fn(a,b)
  if(!identical(schema_a$column_name,schema_b$column_name) || !identical(schema_a$column_type,schema_b$column_type) || any(differences!=0)) stop("Packaged resource does not round-trip to its curated source.")
  if(any(schema_b$column_name %in% config$prohibited_columns)) stop("Prohibited column in packaged resource.")
  rows <- s4a_diagnosis_query_fn(paste0("SELECT count(*) AS n FROM (",b,")")) |> dplyr::collect()
  tibble::tibble(resource=resource$name,rows=rows$n,columns=nrow(schema_b),sha256=row$source_sha256,
    schema_equal=TRUE,rows_equal=TRUE,access=config$access,status=config$status)
}
srelease_schema_fn <- function(paths,root,path) {
  table <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(paths,function(input) {
    schema <- s4a_diagnosis_query_fn(paste("DESCRIBE SELECT * FROM",s4a_diagnosis_read_fn(input))) |> dplyr::collect()
    tibble::tibble(resource=substring(input,nchar(root)+2L),position=seq_len(nrow(schema)),column=schema$column_name,type=schema$column_type)
  }))
  srelease_write_once_fn(table,path)
}
srelease_manifest_fn <- function(checks,resources,config,path) {
  stopifnot(nrow(checks)==length(resources),!anyDuplicated(checks$resource),all(checks$schema_equal & checks$rows_equal))
  stopifnot(all(checks$access==config$access),all(checks$status==config$status))
  if(file.exists(path)) {
    old <- duckplyr::read_parquet_duckdb(path,prudence="stingy") |> dplyr::collect() |> dplyr::arrange(resource)
    if(!isTRUE(all.equal(as.data.frame(old),as.data.frame(dplyr::arrange(checks,resource)),check.attributes=FALSE))) stop("Immutable verification manifest differs.")
    return(path)
  }
  s5_healthshed_write_table_fn(dplyr::arrange(checks,resource),path)
}

  srelease_directory_fn(here::here("data","outputs","releases"),srelease_parameters_list),
  file.path(srelease_directory_fn(here::here("data","outputs","releases"),srelease_parameters_list),"resource_schemas.parquet"))

title: 32  Export the Frictionless Data Package
text:
Extend the versioned candidate from pages 19–21 with datapackage.json in data/outputs/releases/v<MAJOR>.<MINOR>.<BUGFIX>/ (initially v0.1.0). The stable name, semantic version, release notes, resource inventory, native schemas, checksums, and spatial interpretation travel with the data. Rendering declares targets and never packages research data.






Important Prerequisite: Require Independently Verified Parquet Products



Consume the explicit srelease_resources_list, immutable contract, verified resource manifest, and schema inventory from pages 19–21. Do not glob the intermediate directory: unrelated or stale files must not enter the release. The shape audit must pass before the contract can be created. Access remains internal and status candidate; creating a package does not publish it.








Tip Procedure: Record the Direct Parquet Compatibility Experiment



On 2026-11-10, a synthetic Parquet table containing an integer identifier, WKT point, and CRS WKT was supplied unchanged to frictionless::add_resource() in Frictionless 2.0.1. It failed with embedded nul in string: 'PAR1...'. This establishes a reader limitation: add_resource() expects a data frame or delimited-text paths. Passing a data frame instead would cause the writer to serialize CSV.
The fallback uses the standard’s generic Data Resource inside a Data Package v1. The R library’s supported create_package(descriptor) and read_package() interfaces handle the descriptor; JSON serialization writes only metadata. We do not call its CSV-oriented write_package(): that writer also flattens local resource paths, losing the distinct by_diagnosis/ and audits/seams/ directories. Every Parquet file stays at its existing relative path with identical bytes. The compatibility experiment is reproducible in tests/check-frictionless-release.R.








Tip Procedure: Inventory Resources and Preserve Native Schemas



parquetSchema records exact DuckDB column types, including list/struct types; it deliberately avoids claiming that a CSV Table Schema validates Parquet. Generic Frictionless tools can discover resources and metadata, but readers need Parquet support to load their contents. SHA-256 values are recorded as a custom sha256 property, with the algorithm stated explicitly.
The existing healthshed serialization is ordinary Parquet with WKT, not GeoParquet. Its spatial metadata identifies the geometry, CRS, key, empty flag, and reference-year columns. CRS WKT and reference years remain in the table. Reconstruct with sf::st_as_sfc(x$geometry_wkt, crs=x$crs_wkt[[1]]). Reporting and spatial metadata join on clinic_ID; healthsheds use fs_uid. The geometry remains the historical 2022 reference.
srelease_inventory_fn <- function(resources,files,contract,manifest,schemas,config) {
  srelease_parameters_fn(config)
  if(length(files)!=length(resources)) stop("Incomplete packaged resource inventory.")
  root <- dirname(contract)
  records <- c(resources,list(
    list(name="_contract.parquet",source=contract),
    list(name="manifest.parquet",source=manifest),
    list(name="resource_schemas.parquet",source=schemas)))
  names <- vapply(records,`[[`,"","name")
  ids <- gsub("/","--",tools::file_path_sans_ext(names),fixed=TRUE)
  if(anyDuplicated(names) || anyDuplicated(ids) || any(!grepl("^[a-z0-9._-]+$",ids))) stop("Resource names collide or are invalid.")
  checks <- duckplyr::read_parquet_duckdb(manifest,prudence="stingy") |> dplyr::collect()
  if(nrow(checks)!=length(resources) || anyDuplicated(checks$resource) ||
     !setequal(checks$resource,names[seq_along(resources)]) ||
     !isTRUE(all(checks$schema_equal & checks$rows_equal))) stop("Independent verification is incomplete.")
  lapply(seq_along(records),function(i) {
    record <- records[[i]]
    if(grepl("^/|(^|/)\\.\\.(/|$)|\\\\",record$name)) stop("Unsafe resource path.")
    path <- file.path(root,record$name)
    if(!file.exists(path) || !identical(srelease_sha256_fn(path),srelease_sha256_fn(record$source))) stop("Resource differs from its curated source.")
    if(i<=length(resources)) {
      expected <- checks$sha256[match(record$name,checks$resource)]
      if(!identical(srelease_sha256_fn(path),expected) ||
         !normalizePath(path) %in% normalizePath(files)) stop("Resource differs from verified manifest.")
    }
    sql <- paste("SELECT * FROM",s4a_diagnosis_read_fn(path))
    schema <- s4a_diagnosis_query_fn(paste("DESCRIBE",sql)) |> dplyr::collect()
    rows <- s4a_diagnosis_query_fn(paste0("SELECT count(*) AS n FROM (",sql,")")) |> dplyr::collect()
    resource <- list(profile="data-resource",name=ids[[i]],path=record$name,
      title=gsub("_"," ",tools::file_path_sans_ext(record$name),fixed=TRUE),
      format="parquet",mediatype="application/vnd.apache.parquet",
      bytes=unname(file.info(path)$size),sha256=srelease_sha256_fn(path),
      rowCount=as.numeric(rows$n),
      role=if(i>length(resources)) "release-metadata" else if(startsWith(record$name,"audits/")) "audit" else "data-or-provenance",
      parquetSchema=lapply(seq_len(nrow(schema)),function(j)
        list(name=schema$column_name[[j]],type=schema$column_type[[j]])))
    if(identical(record$name,"healthsheds2022.parquet")) {
      required <- c("fs_uid","geometry_wkt","crs_wkt","is_empty","reference_year")
      if(!all(required %in% schema$column_name)) stop("Missing spatial interpretation fields.")
      resource$spatial <- list(encoding="WKT",geometryColumn="geometry_wkt",
        crsColumn="crs_wkt",primaryKey="fs_uid",emptyColumn="is_empty",
        referenceYearColumn="reference_year",referenceYear=2022L,
        geoparquet=FALSE)
    }
    resource
  })
}
srelease_descriptor_fn <- function(inventory,config) {
  srelease_parameters_fn(config)
  frictionless::create_package(list(profile="data-package",name=config$name,
    title=config$title,version=config$version,
    description="Curated Madagascar clinic diagnoses, reporting and spatial metadata, historical healthsheds, and provenance/audits in canonical Parquet.",
    access=config$access,status=config$status,
    releaseNotes=config$notes,change=config$change,previousVersion=config$previous_version,
    versionPolicy="MAJOR: breaking changes for external collaborators; MINOR: non-breaking changes; PATCH: bug fixes.",
    validation=list(descriptor="Frictionless R create/read package checks; not full JSON Schema validation",
      data="SHA-256, DuckDB native schema and complete row-multiset verification in pages 19-21",
      checksumAlgorithm="sha256",parquetReader="DuckDB",spatialReader="sf (WKT + CRS WKT)"),
    resources=inventory))
}








Tip Procedure: Atomically Write and Reopen the Descriptor



The only added file is datapackage.json. Equal-content retries succeed; changed metadata or data under an existing version fail. Sources and package copies are checked again even when the descriptor already exists. No timestamp is generated on retry. Resource contents remain covered by the independent page-21 verifier and SHA-256 checks; Frictionless’s package checks alone do not validate Parquet cells or scientific meaning.
srelease_datapackage_fn <- function(inventory,config,root) {
  package <- srelease_descriptor_fn(inventory,config)
  directory <- srelease_directory_fn(root,config)
  if(!dir.exists(directory)) stop("Verified candidate directory does not exist.")
  for(resource in inventory) {
    path <- file.path(directory,resource$path)
    if(!identical(srelease_sha256_fn(path),resource$sha256)) stop("Packaged resource changed before descriptor export.")
  }
  encoded <- jsonlite::toJSON(package,auto_unbox=TRUE,pretty=TRUE,null="null",na="null",digits=NA)
  destination <- file.path(directory,"datapackage.json")
  if(file.exists(destination)) {
    if(!identical(paste(readLines(destination,warn=FALSE),collapse="\n"),as.character(encoded))) stop("Immutable descriptor differs; choose a new release version.")
    return(destination)
  }
  temporary <- tempfile(".datapackage-",tmpdir=directory,fileext=".json")
  on.exit(unlink(temporary),add=TRUE)
  writeLines(encoded,temporary,useBytes=TRUE)
  restored <- frictionless::read_package(temporary)
  expected <- jsonlite::fromJSON(encoded,simplifyVector=FALSE)
  observed <- jsonlite::fromJSON(temporary,simplifyVector=FALSE)
  if(!identical(expected,observed) ||
     !identical(frictionless::resource_names(restored),vapply(inventory,`[[`,"","name"))) stop("Descriptor round trip failed.")
  if(!file.rename(temporary,destination)) stop("Could not install the descriptor atomically.")
  destination
}
srelease_inventory_list <- srelease_inventory_fn(srelease_resources_list,srelease_package_parquet,
  srelease_contract_parquet,srelease_manifest_parquet,srelease_schema_parquet,srelease_parameters_list)
#| format: file
srelease_datapackage_json <- srelease_datapackage_fn(srelease_inventory_list,
  srelease_parameters_list,here::here("data","outputs","releases"))
The final target depends on the independent verification manifest and native schema inventory. To export a release, review the page-19 parameters and run the following inside a compute-node allocation:

Distribute the entire version directory: relative resource paths make it relocatable. Consumers can inspect datapackage.json using frictionless::read_package() and load a selected resource using duckplyr::read_parquet_duckdb(file.path(release_directory, resource$path)). frictionless::read_resource() is not the Parquet reader.
